papers.title: Conversion hip arthroplasty has a higher risk of venous thromboembolism disease at 30 days than primary total hip arthroplasty and revision total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Venous thromboembolic disease (VTED), including deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), represents a serious postoperative complication following total hip arthroplasty (THA). While revision THA is traditionally considered higher risk than primary THA, the thromboembolic risks of conversion THA are still not well defined. This study compared 30-day DVT rates across primary, conversion, and revision THA. METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional analysis was performed using the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database. Adult patients undergoing primary, conversion, or revision THA were identified using Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes. A total of 475,002 patients met inclusion criteria (primary THA: 428,245 [90.2%], conversion THA: 10,637 [2.2%], revision THA: 36,120 [7.6%]) with a mean age of 65.6 years (range, 18 to 89); 55.0% women. The primary outcome was 30-day postoperative DVT. Multivariable logistic regressions evaluated associations between procedure type and DVT, adjusting for age, sex, BMI, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class, smoking status, chronic steroid use, and operating time. RESULTS: = 0.014) compared with conversion THA. Independent predictors of higher DVT risk included older age, longer operating time, and chronic steroid use. Sex, BMI, ASA class, and smoking status were not independently associated with DVT. CONCLUSIONS: Conversion THA is associated with higher 30-day DVT risk compared with both primary and revision THA on multivariable analyses. Recognition of conversion THA as a distinct procedural category associated with higher relative thromboembolic risk may improve perioperative risk stratification and guide more individualised thromboprophylaxis strategies.

papers.title: Robot-assisted total hip arthroplasty for Crowe type II or higher hip dysplasia
papers.abstract: Robot-assisted total hip arthroplasty (RATHA) offers superior implant accuracy, but its efficacy for highly deformed hips remains unclear. This study compared the RATHA outcomes of patients with Crowe types II–IV and I osteoarthritis. We evaluated 25 hips that underwent RATHA for Crowe types II–IV osteoarthritis (Crowe II–IV group). Propensity score matching (age, sex, and body mass index) was used to select 75 matched hips with Crowe type I osteoarthritis (Crowe I group). The outcomes included component positioning, distance from teardrop to femoral head centre, operative data, complications, and Harris Hip Scores. The absolute navigation errors of the groups did not differ significantly (Crowe II–IV: radiographic inclination [RI] 1.6 ± 1.7°, radiographic inclination [RA] 1.7 ± 2.1°; Crowe I: RI 1.3 ± 1.3°, RA 1.4 ± 2.0°). However, the vertical distance from the teardrop to the femoral head centre was significantly greater for the Crowe II–IV group than for the Crowe I group (23.6 ± 6.4 mm vs. 19.8 ± 4.4 mm, P = 0.001). A vertical distance of > 28 mm was observed for four Crowe II–IV cases (16%), but not for the Crowe I group. The postoperative Harris Hip Score and complication rates did not differ significantly. RATHA for Crowe type II–IV osteoarthritis achieved accurate implant alignment comparable to that for Crowe type I. However, superior displacement of the hip joint centre occurred in 16% of severe cases, suggesting caution for inferior acetabular osteophytes. The similar complication rates support the clinical utility of RATHA even for severe deformities.

papers.title: Thermal Behavior, Densification Mechanism and Processing Optimization of CuCrZr Fabricated by Selective Laser Melting: Simulation and Experiment
papers.abstract: Selective laser melting (SLM) technology enables the precise manufacture of complex‐structured parts. However, the high laser reflectivity of CuCrZr alloy presents significant challenges to achieving high‐quality forming. This paper integrates numerical simulation with experimental investigations to optimize the SLM process parameters for the alloy and explore the underlying mechanism of defect formation. Ansys APDL software is employed to establish a model of CuCrZr alloy fabricated by SLM, and a numerical simulation‐based analytical approach for molten pool overlap is proposed. The effects of laser power and scanning speed on the relative density and defect formation of CuCrZr alloy are systematically investigated. The results demonstrate that when the laser power was 330 W and the scanning speed was 700 mm/s, the relative density of the prepared sample reached 99.78%. The microstructure of the CuCrZr alloy is predominantly composed of deformed grains; the grains exhibit a preferred orientation along the <110> direction, and a strong {110} texture is present in the microstructure. Cr elements are uniformly dispersed within the matrix.

papers.title: Evolution of dental implant coatings and functional surfaces: from antimicrobial to immunoactive technologies
papers.abstract: Relevance . Advances in implant surface modification technologies are a key focus of modern implant dentistry. Implant surface modification is being investigated as a way to influence cell adhesion, bone formation, and bacterial colonization. However, experimental findings on new coatings do not allow direct conclusions about their effects on long-term implant survival or the incidence of peri-implant complications. Objective . To analyze current types of dental implant coatings and functional surfaces, their application methods, surface characteristics, and biological effects, and to identify promising directions for further development. Materials and methods. A systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. The review included original experimental studies reporting the implant substrate material, coating type, application method, surface characteristics, and biological assessment. Review articles, duplicate publications, and studies without experimental data were excluded. PubMed/MEDLINE, eLibrary, CyberLeninka and Google Scholar were searched for the period 2015–2026, and the reference lists of studies relevant to the review topic were examined. The search was restricted to original studies available in full text. Search terms were combined to improve search precision: “implants,” “dental implants,” “implant coatings,” “implant surface modification,” “antimicrobial coatings,” “bioactive coatings,” “implant osseointegration,” and “nanostructured surfaces.” Both Russian terms and their English equivalents were used. Risk of bias was assessed using the risk-of-bias tool for preclinical dental materials research (RoBDEMAT), the Systematic Review Centre for Laboratory Animal Experimentation risk-of-bias tool (SYRCLE RoB), or the revised risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2.0), depending on the study type. Results . The final analysis included 31 studies published in 2014–2026. Most studies used in vitro and in vivo experimental models, with only one clinical study included ( n =1). Conclusion. The reviewed studies primarily characterize the biological activity of functional coatings in laboratory and animal models. Their findings do not establish a clinical advantage of new antimicrobial and immunomodulatory coatings in terms of peri-implant complication rates or implant survival. The evidence is insufficient to support widespread clinical use of these coatings. Reproducible preclinical evaluation and comparative clinical studies with long-term follow-up are needed.

papers.title: Morphometric Assessment of Maxillary Posterior Teeth and Sinus Floor Relationships Using Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT): Implications for Immediate Implant Placement
papers.abstract: Objectives: The objective of this study was to validate the classification given by Yun-Hoa Jung in the population of Kheda district (Gujarat, India) and evaluate bone available for immediate implant placement in the maxillary posterior teeth (1st pre molar ,2nd premolar and 1st molar) region. Materials and Method: This observational study evaluated a total of 59 maxillary posterior CBCTs, each having maxillary posterior teeth. CARESTREAM 3D version 3.10.27 and CARESTREAM 3D lite version 3.10.23 was used to view data. All the CBCTs were taken by a qualified specialist and DICOM files were evaluated. Orthogonal slicing and curved slicing views were used to measure the bone available. Results: This study observed that the distobuccal (DB) roots of the maxillary first molar were closest to the sinus floor followed by the mesiobuccal (MB) and palatal roots. The palatal roots of maxillary first premolar were closer than the buccal roots. Type 2 and Type 3 relationships were found to be highly prevalent (67.8% combined) in the first molar region. Conclusion: Preoperative CBCT analysis using the Jung’s classification is essential for identifying patients with low available bone height (Types 2 and 3). For these patients, immediate implant placement may require adjunctive procedures like sinus floor elevation to ensure long-term success. Clinical Relevance: Preoperative cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) analysis using the Jung’s classification is crucial in the maxillary posterior region to identify the vertical relationship of the tooth apex and the floor of the maxillary sinus. Recognizing these anatomical variations allow clinicians to anticipate limited bone height and strategically plan adjunctive procedures, such as sinus floor elevation, bone grafting etc. to ensure primary stability and long-term implant success. Consequently, integrating this classification system into diagnostic workflows optimizes treatment predictability and mitigates the risk of Schneiderian membrane perforation during immediate implant placement.

papers.title: Magnetic field superposition mechanism and multi-objective optimization of a dual-excitation permanent magnet vernier motor
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a dual-excitation permanent magnet vernier motor (DE-PMVM) with permanent magnets mounted on both the stator and the rotor. The magnetic field superposition mechanism and electromagnetic performance are systematically analyzed, and a multi-objective optimization design is carried out. First, through analytical derivation and finite element method, the spatial linear superposition characteristics of air-gap flux density under the dual-excitation structure are revealed within the normal operating range, which is physically rooted in the dominance of the air-gap reluctance in the magnetic circuit. On this basis, a multi-objective optimization framework combining a Kriging surrogate model and the multi-objective genetic algorithm (MOGA) algorithm is established, with the objectives of maximizing the average torque and minimizing the torque ripple, to synergistically optimize the coverage ratio, thickness, and magnetization ratio of the rotor permanent magnets. The results show that the optimized motor achieves a 10.575% increase in torque, and the torque ripple is reduced as well, indicating the effectiveness and potential engineering practicality of the proposed method. This paper provides a theoretical basis and engineering reference for the analysis and design of high-torque-density, low-torque-ripple permanent magnet vernier motors.

papers.title: Data Driven Design of Alginate Hydrogels for the Delivery of Spinal Cord Injury Therapeutics
papers.abstract: Hydrogels are among the most versatile platforms for controlled drug delivery, yet identifying a formulation that produces a desired release profile remains a slow, largely empirical process. This is particularly limiting for alginate, whose release behavior emerges from the nonlinear interplay of polymer molecular weight, concentration, guluronate content, crosslinking cation, and gelation kinetics. This dissertation develops and validates an automated, machine learning-guided framework that navigates this design space efficiently and then applies it to two fragile biologics relevant to spinal cord injury (SCI): the matrix-degrading enzyme chondroitinase ABC (chABC) and the neurotrophin brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF). Using a liquid-handling robot, a seed library of 120 alginate formulations loaded with bovine serum albumin (BSA) was prepared and its release measured. A Gaussian process regression model, trained under an implicit scheme to predict cumulative release over time, was interrogated with Shapley additive explanations, which identified time, alginate molecular weight, and alginate concentration as the dominant determinants of release. Bayesian active learning with an expected-improvement acquisition function then drove successive formulation generations toward near zero-order kinetics. Critically, the top BSA-optimized formulations transferred without further optimization to the sustained release of active chABC single-enzyme nanoparticles (chABC-SENs), demonstrating that surrogate-derived formulations generalize to a labile therapeutic enzyme. To enable minimally invasive co-delivery, four clinically relevant shear-thinning hydrogels were screened for chABC-SEN compatibility. Hydrophobically associated networks abolished enzymatic activity, whereas a hydrophilic alginate-hyaluronic acid (alg-HA) matrix preserved it, establishing hydrophobicity as a critical and previously underappreciated design parameter. The alg-HA platform supported sustained co-release of active chABC-SEN alongside immunoreactive BDNF, which followed a biphasic profile reaching approximately 78% by day 11. Together, these studies deliver a generalizable, data-driven strategy for hydrogel formulation optimization and a compatible injectable vehicle for co-delivering a matrix-degrading enzyme and a neurotrophic factor, providing a foundation for combination therapies for spinal cord injury.

papers.title: Open Core Decompression with Allograft Impaction for Femoral Head Osteonecrosis: A Light Bulb Technique Approach
papers.abstract: Background: Osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH), also known as avascular necrosis (AVN), is a debilitating condition characterized by the death of bone tissue due to an inadequate blood supply. This pathology predominantly affects young adults, with the average age at treatment ranging from 33 to 38 years, and often leads to the destruction of the hip joint, necessitating total hip arthroplasty (THA) Methods: The study was conducted as a prospective observational analysis of patients diagnosed with femoral head osteonecrosis (Stages 2B and 3 Ficat) who underwent open core decompression combined with cancellous allograft impaction using the light bulb technique. The inclusion criteria were patients aged between 20 and 55 years with symptomatic osteonecrosis of the femoral head, classified as Stage 2B or 3 according to the Ficat and Arlet classification.. Exclusion criteria consisted of patients with advanced arthritis (Stage 4 ONFH), previous surgical intervention for osteonecrosis, significant hip deformity, inflammatory arthropathies, metabolic bone disease. Results: A total of 46 patients (58 hips) were included in the study. The mean follow-up duration was 5 years (range: 3–7 years). Of the total patients, 28 were male (60.9%) and 18 were female (39.1%), with a mean age of 37.5 years (range: 24–54 years). The most common etiology of osteonecrosis was corticosteroid use (43.5%), followed by alcohol consumption (30.4%) and idiopathic causes (26.1%). Conclusion: Open core decompression with allograft impaction using the light bulb technique is an effective treatment for intermediate-stage FHO. This approach provides significant functional improvement, pain relief, and delays the need for THA, particularly in stage 2B cases. Future studies with larger sample sizes and longer follow-up periods are needed to further validate these findings.

papers.title: Linking Scaffold Architecture, Ion Transport and Biofilm Formation in Functionalized TPMS Scaffolds Using a Digital Twin Framework
papers.abstract: Abstract Periprosthetic infections remain a major complication of orthopedic implants despite advances in antimicrobial surface functionalization. While antibacterial coatings can reduce bacterial colonization, local transport phenomena within porous implant architectures may generate spatially heterogeneous antimicrobial exposure, potentially influencing biofilm persistence. This study developed and experimentally validated a digital twin (DT) framework integrating scaffold morphology, computational fluid dynamics, antimicrobial ion transport, and bacterial colonization modelling to investigate the relationship between scaffold architecture and antibacterial performance. Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) hydroxyapatite scaffolds with gyroid and diamond architectures were fabricated and functionalized with an Ag–ZnO/HA nanocomposite coating. DT predictions were validated using micro-CT, SEM/EDS, ICP-OES, confocal laser scanning microscopy, microbiological assays, and quantitative PCR under dynamic perfusion bioreactor conditions. The gyroid architecture demonstrated superior antibacterial performance, achieving a 4.15 ± 0.41 log reduction in adherent bacteria compared with 3.42 ± 0.48 log for the diamond scaffold. CLSM revealed sparse, dispersed bacterial colonization in gyroid scaffolds, whereas diamond structures exhibited localized biofilm accumulation in regions associated with reduced transport. DT predictions showed good agreement with experimental observations (R² = 0.84). Bacteria recovered from low-transport regions of diamond scaffolds exhibited modest increases in Ag⁺ MIC and activation of stress-response pathways, indicating adaptive physiological responses under heterogeneous antimicrobial exposure. Virtual optimization identified an improved gyroid configuration with a reduced unit cell size (350 μm). Experimental validation confirmed lower biofilm accumulation, more uniform Ag⁺ distribution, and enhanced antibacterial performance without increasing antimicrobial loading. These findings demonstrate that scaffold topology influences antibacterial efficacy through its effect on local transport conditions and highlight the potential of digital twin methodologies as a supportive tool for the design and evaluation of antibacterial bone scaffolds.

papers.title: Advances in 3D‐Printed Scaffolds for Regenerative Therapy
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Three‐dimensional (3D) printing enables precise control over scaffold geometry, porosity, material distribution, and spatial delivery of cells and bioactive cues. However, features intended to improve biological fidelity often increase manufacturing complexity, quality‐control demands, and regulatory burden. This review evaluates 3D‐printed scaffolds for regenerative therapy using a design‐to‐translation framework. We compare acellular printing, cell‐laden bioprinting, and hybrid fabrication, and examine how material composition, architecture, mechanics, degradation, gradients, vascularization, innervation, and immune integration determine performance. Evidence is synthesized across cartilage and osteochondral repair, bone, skin, neural, and spinal cord repair, skeletal muscle and soft tissues, and cardiac and vascular regeneration. Current evidence places acellular or minimally bioactive patient‐specific scaffolds closest to clinical adoption, particularly when anatomical conformity and structural support are the dominant requirements. By contrast, living bioprinted constructs remain limited by reproducibility, tissue maturation, safety, storage, release testing, and scalable manufacturing. We therefore propose that scaffold complexity should be matched to a defined biological bottleneck and assessed using endpoints that capture functional repair, interface stability, host integration, and long‐term performance. This framework shifts evaluation beyond printability toward regenerative benefit, manufacturability, and clinically reproducible design.

papers.title: Orthopaedic Implants in the Oncologic and Irradiated Bone Environment: A Review
papers.abstract: Patients who require an orthopaedic implant after cancer treatment present four linked problems: a bone bed damaged by radiotherapy or chemotherapy, large reconstructions under high mechanical load, a high risk of infection, and hardware that degrades the imaging and radiotherapy planning on which oncologic follow-up depends. This narrative review examines how each problem alters implant performance and which design responses have clinical support. Radiotherapy roughly doubles dental implant failure, is associated with loosening, infection, and periprosthetic fracture after arthroplasty, and leads to non-union in most radiation-associated femoral fractures treated by internal fixation. Deep infection affects about one in ten tumour endoprostheses. Additively manufactured porous titanium and porous tantalum support bone ingrowth, but follow-up rarely exceeds five years, and their large surface area may favour bacterial colonisation. Silver, iodine, and antibiotic-loaded hydrogel coatings are associated with fewer infections in observational studies, with low certainty. Carbon-fibre-reinforced polyetheretherketone (PEEK) reduces imaging artefact and dose perturbation, and biodegradable magnesium avoids hardware removal, but neither has a proven advantage in oncologic reconstruction. Throughout, evidence is labelled by its source—oncologic, extrapolated, or preclinical—and the comparative studies still needed are specified.

papers.title: Osteogenic Gene Expression of Human Mesenchymal Stromal Cells on Additively Manufactured Porous Titanium: Implications for Graft-Sparing Spine Implant Strategies
papers.abstract: Additively manufactured porous titanium implants are increasingly used in spine surgery; however, it remains unclear whether porous titanium substrates can support osteogenic transcriptional programs without supplemental bone graft material. This study evaluated osteogenic gene expression in primary human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells cultured on additively manufactured porous Ti6Al4V lattice discs and geometry-matched solid Ti6Al4V controls with identical surface treatments, including grit blasting, nano-hydroxyapatite coating, and alkali etching. Smooth Ti6Al4V served as the reference substrate. Cell attachment was assessed qualitatively by fluorescence imaging, and osteogenic gene expression was quantified by qRT-PCR at Days 7 and 14 for RUNX2, ALPL, COL1A1, SPP1, and BGLAP relative to basal and osteogenically induced controls. Fluorescence staining was consistent with MSC attachment on porous titanium, while elongated individual cells were clearly resolved on solid controls. ALPL was robustly induced across titanium groups at both time points, indicating sustained early osteogenic activity, while COL1A1 remained detectable, supporting ongoing matrix-associated transcription. The robust and sustained ALPL induction observed here is consistent with its established role as a reliable indicator of early-to-intermediate osteogenic progression in vitro. In a parallel multi-marker qRT-PCR profiling study of human BM-MSCs on 3D-printed porous scaffolds under osteogenic induction at Days 7 and 14, ALPL was the most consistently elevated marker and was classified as an early-stage osteogenic readout, confirming its value as the primary transcriptional indicator. Importantly, ALPL induction at Day 14 on both porous and solid Ti6Al4V surfaces suggests that titanium substrates can sustain early enzyme-associated differentiation signaling under osteogenic induction without supplemental graft material. RUNX2 expression was modest, consistent with early lineage commitment, and SPP1 showed time- and condition-dependent changes. BGLAP levels remained low within the Day 7–14 window, suggesting that terminal maturation was not captured. These findings indicate that additively manufactured porous titanium provides a permissive microenvironment that supports staged osteogenic gene expression in human MSCs and supports the feasibility of graft-sparing spine implant strategies.

papers.title: Thermal Variational Deep Material Networks: Physics-based surrogates for heat transport under microstructural uncertainty
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous microstructures such as woven composites, sintered materials, and additively manufactured parts exhibit unavoidable morphological variability that can produce a significant spread of effective thermal responses. The goal of this work is a physics-based surrogate that learns the distribution of the effective conductivity over a family of statistically equivalent microstructures and propagates it to the temperature field of a component, without solving a microscale boundary value problem for each realization. To that effect, we extend the Variational Deep Material Network (VDMN) framework, originally developed for mechanical homogenization, to thermal conduction and integrate it into a multiscale scheme where a macroscale finite element (FE) solver is supplied with stochastic effective conductivity information by VDMN (FE-VDMN). The thermal VDMN represents variability through probability distributions over the geometric parameters of its hierarchical laminate building blocks and analytically propagates the first two cumulants of these distributions to the mean and covariance of the effective conductivity tensor. In this way, stochastic thermal homogenization is recast as inference and cumulant propagation on a reduced network representation. For spinodal and superalloy-like microstructure families, the thermal VDMN reproduces the mean and a calibrated joint distribution of the effective conductivity components over a broad range of phase contrast. Demonstrated at the component scale, FE-VDMN propagates this distribution to the temperature field at a fraction of the cost of classical FE 2 schemes, which require a new microscale solve for every microstructure realization. This framework provides a computationally tractable route for uncertainty-aware multiscale thermal simulation, with FE-FFT reference comparisons included to assess accuracy and computational cost.

papers.title: Unsupervised statistical learning for die analysis in ancient numismatics
papers.abstract: Die analysis is an essential numismatic method, and an important tool of ancient economic history. Yet, manual die studies are too labor-intensive to comprehensively study large coinages such as those of the Roman Empire. We address this problem by proposing a model for unsupervised computational die analysis, which can reduce the time investment necessary for large-scale die studies by several orders of magnitude, in many cases from years to weeks. From a computer vision viewpoint, die studies present a challenging unsupervised clustering problem, because they involve an unknown and large number of highly similar semantic classes of imbalanced sizes. We address these issues through determining dissimilarities between coin faces derived from specifically devised Gaussian process-based keypoint features in a Bayesian distance clustering framework. The efficacy of our method is demonstrated through an analysis of 1135 Roman silver coins struck between 64-66 C.E..

papers.title: Global gridded air-sea oxygen flux inferred from a machine learning-based dissolved oxygen product
papers.abstract: We present estimates of the monthly open ocean air-sea O 2 flux from 2004 to 2024 on a 1 ° ×1° grid spanning 64.5° S to 79.5° N. The flux is computed using 4-dimensional ocean dissolved oxygen (DO) fields derived from Argo float and shipboard observations via machine learning algorithms (GOBAI-O 2 , Sharp et al., 2023). Flux uncertainties are quantified by generating a large ensemble of flux estimates, first propagating errors from the dissolved oxygen product, then computing fluxes across all combinations of three gas exchange parameterizations that account for bubble-mediated flux and three wind products. We apply DO adjustments to align our resolved global annual mean fluxes with those derived from scaling global ocean heat uptake and regional annual mean fluxes with those derived from ocean inversions. Our results show larger seasonal flux variations at high latitudes than at low latitudes, with clear differences between major ocean basins. Both adjusted and unadjusted annual mean flux estimates exhibit strong ocean O 2 sinks at high latitudes, weak sources in the low-to-mid latitude subtropics, and weak sinks near the Equator. The annual mean adjustment enhances ocean O 2 uptake in the northern high latitudes and reduces outgassing in the tropics and northern subtropics, while slightly weakening uptake in the Southern Ocean. We evaluate our flux seasonal cycles and annual mean values by comparing forward transport simulations with atmospheric O 2 observations from global airborne surveys and surface sampling stations. The simulations reproduce the observed mean seasonal cycles well, but some differences remain in the annual mean latitudinal gradients. We analyze fractional variance contributions from DO, wind, and gas exchange scheme uncertainties and their interactions at regional and hemispheric scales for both climatological monthly and annual mean fluxes. This dataset marks a major improvement over existing air-sea O 2 flux products, as it includes the resolution of interannual variability in the flux seasonal cycle, the use of advanced machine learning-based DO fields that better represent complex spatial and temporal patterns, and robust uncertainty quantification across various scales. papers.title: Physics-guided deep learning for high resolution X-ray free-electron laser imaging
papers.abstract: Imperfections in X-ray imaging systems can limit their performance, especially in High Energy Density (HED) or Inertial Fusion Energy (IFE)-relevant experiments that are typically single shot, by introducing structured, non-stationary features that overlap with the signal of interest. When the X-ray transmission is reconstructed by typical flat-field normalization, even small shot-to-shot drift of structured features imprints residual patterns onto transmission maps, degrading signal visibility and biasing measurements such as electron density, velocity and feature sizes. We investigate this limitation by modeling the artifacts as a separable feature layer and training a U-Net architecture to estimate and infer them directly from the experimental data. We compare our method against Fourier filtering and more advanced procedures like Dynamic Flat-Field Normalization (DFFN) to evaluate artifact suppression capability and signal preservation in the reconstructed transmission maps. In multiple synthetic injection tests, our Physics-Guided Deep Learning approach is able to obtain an improvement in mean Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) from 0.345 to 0.906 and from 0.0679 to 0.945, while better preserving filament profiles and reducing degradation of the filament signal during artifact suppression. Additionally, we utilize deep ensembles to obtain predictive epistemic uncertainty estimates for the U-Net based reconstruction, to ensure Out Of Distribution (OOD) robustness for this procedure.

papers.title: The stippled grid points are statistically significant: (mis)uses of false discovery rate correction for geospatial data
papers.abstract: Peer-reviewed articles in the geosciences routinely assess statistical significance in spatially distributed data. Statistical significance is often assessed independently at each grid point, while formal adjustment for multiple testing is applied less consistently. Although several approaches to account for multiple testing exist, their application to geosciences data is not always straightforward, as these data often exhibit spatially coherent signals. In this work we revisit the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) false discovery rate (FDR) correction, which is a commonly used method to account for multiple testing, in the context of spatially structured datasets. We first highlight how neglecting multiple-testing correction can substantially inflate the number of false positives. We further show that the BH correction approach proposed in literature for application in geosciences can yield counterintuitive results when applied to spatially coherent signals that cover large fractions of a spatial domain. To illustrate the latter point, we provide an example based on near-surface air temperature composites following sudden stratospheric warmings. We show that when anomalies are spatially coherent, restricting the spatial domain can increase the BH-corrected significance threshold. Consequently, the same underlying field can display a larger number of statistically significant grid points solely due to domain selection, despite unchanged data. We explain this behavior from the point of view of the rank-based structure of the BH correction and discuss its implications for spatial inference and uncertainty quantification in the geosciences. Furthermore, a numerical experiment confirms that the larger the fraction of true positives the higher the BH-corrected significance threshold becomes for a set FDR level. Building on these insights, we outline practical recommendations for transparent and robust significance assessment in geoscientific applications. These include clearly documenting multiple-testing corrections when adjusted pointwise significance is shown, cautious interpretation of adjusted thresholds, careful avoidance of a posteriori domain selection and considering spatially aware alternatives such as regional or cluster-based inference when appropriate. Overall, our results highlight both the need to account for multiple-testing, and potential issues with a naïve application and interpretation of the BH correction. We hope that our work may contribute to more robust statistical testing in the geosciences.

papers.title: Machine Learning for Heterogeneous Data Integration: Analysis of Recent Advances, Open Challenges and Problems, and Practical Deployment Guidance
papers.abstract: The challenge of large-scale applications nowadays is that they must merge structured, semi-structured, and unstructured information of various sources. Machine learning auto-aligns schemas, matches entities, and fuses semantics, reducing manual effort and making it more scalable. We critically review the 2024–2026 improvements in eight method families: schema matching, representation learning, deep learning and graph neural networks, knowledge graphs, transfer learning, active learning, large language models and multi-source fusion. There are three findings that stand out. To start with, there is no one family that is dominant in all situations: each of them has to make a trade-off between precision and label requirements, cost, interpretability, or transferability, and more transferable results are more likely to be expensive to compute. Second, interpretability is not available in most families except knowledge-graph and active-learning schemes, which is a significant impediment in controlled areas. Third, hybrid pipelines are a promising design principle, but end-to-end evidence is limited: only domain generalization followed by active learning has been evaluated as a complete pipeline, whereas others, such as contrastive blocking followed by LLM matching, remain design suggestions supported at the component level. We translate these findings into scenario-based deployment guidance and identify six cross-cutting open challenges, including unstructured heterogeneity, uncertainty quantification, scalability, label efficiency, fairness, and privacy. Researchers and practitioners should find this analysis useful as a structured assessment of where ML-enabled integration stands and where it is heading.

papers.title: Measured-PV Converter-Loss-Aware Model Predictive Smart Charging and Vehicle-to-Grid Control for Electric Vehicle Fleets Under Forecast Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Variable solar availability and bidirectional-converter losses complicate the coordination of electric-vehicle (EV) charging and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) services. This study computationally assesses a receding-horizon model predictive control (MPC) strategy using irradiance measurements collected at the Microgrid Laboratory of Universidad de Cuenca, Ecuador. The laboratory dataset provides minute-resolution irradiance records; photovoltaic (PV) power is estimated using a 35 kWp reference system rather than measured at an operating charging site. A 24 h simulation with two bidirectional EV chargers compares uncontrolled, solar-smart, rule-based V2G and MPC-V2G scheduling under the same scenario-based facility load and EV sessions. In the deterministic case, MPC reduces peak grid import from 24.51 to 12.77 kW (47.9%) and grid import from 184.36 to 147.88 kWh (19.8%) relative to uncontrolled charging. Thirty paired stochastic runs achieve 100% modeled departure-target satisfaction and a lower mean peak with MPC. The controller uses nominal conversion efficiencies; a load-dependent map quantifies conversion losses after dispatch. Peak mitigation entails increased battery throughput, and the reported results are computational rather than hardware or field validation.

papers.title: Multi-model XAI framework for prediabetes and diabetes risk stratification using population-level health indicators
papers.abstract: Introduction Diabetes mellitus is a globally prevalent chronic metabolic disorder whose timely identification is critical to preventing irreversible end-organ damage. Although machine learning (ML) approaches have shown considerable promise for automated diabetes screening, the field is hampered by methodological deficiencies — notably data leakage during preprocessing and oversampler selection performed outside cross-validation folds — that collectively produce overoptimistic and clinically unreliable performance estimates. Methods We present a rigorously leakage-aware, multi-stage ML pipeline evaluated on a large-scale publicly available synthetic clinical dataset comprising 100,000 records and 15 features (prevalence 8.5%). The pipeline explicitly addresses two categories of leakage: (i) preprocessing leakage , by fitting all transformers exclusively on training data; and (ii) resampling leakage , by performing oversampler comparison entirely within cross-validation folds. The pipeline encompasses: (i) stratified three-way splitting into training, calibration, and held-out test partitions; (ii) an in-fold cross-validated comparison of seven resampling strategies against a no-resampling class-weighted baseline, with SMOTETomek selected automatically on cross-validated F1; (iii) training of four base classifiers (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, HistGradientBoosting, LightGBM); (iv) six model-fusion strategies; (v) isotonic probability calibration; (vi) decision curve analysis; and (vii) Mondrian class-conditional split-conformal prediction. Results Among all models, LightGBM, HistGradientBoosting, and the logarithmic pooling fusion ensemble (Fus-LogPool) achieved statistically equivalent top performance: PR-AUC of 0.8807 (Fus-LogPool), 0.8801 (LightGBM), and 0.8798 (HistGB), with pairwise McNemar tests uniformly non-significant ( p > 0.5), indicating that a simple well-tuned single gradient-boosted tree is as effective as fusion on this dataset. Mondrian conformal prediction attained 90.39% empirical coverage (target 90%), with 98.82% singleton predictions and singleton accuracy of 91.46%. Decision curve analysis confirmed net clinical benefit over treat-all and treat-none strategies across clinically relevant risk thresholds (5%–20%). SHAP global explanations identified HbA1c level, blood glucose level, BMI, and age as the dominant risk determinants. Discussion Importantly, all findings derive from a synthetic or semi-synthetic dataset without a verified clinical source, and must be validated on prospective real-world cohorts before any clinical application. The fully reproducible pipeline is released as an open-source Kaggle notebook.

papers.title: Research on GLCC liquid level-pressure control method based on NMPC with channel-decoupled multi-residual consistency monitoring
papers.abstract: Abstract To address the strong coupling between liquid level and pressure, rapid dynamic response, and actuator lag in a gas-liquid cylindrical cyclone (GLCC) separator under inlet slug-flow disturbances, this paper proposes a coordinated level-pressure control method that combines nonlinear model predictive control NMPC as the primary controller with parallel monitoring by a shadow PID controller. First, a nonlinear dynamic model of GLCC liquid level and pressure is established based on mass conservation and the ideal-gas equation of state, and first-order valve actuation dynamics are incorporated into the closed-loop simulation plant. Second, an NMPC controller is designed to coordinate liquid-level and pressure regulation. On this basis, a shadow PID controller is introduced as a background reference controller, and a normalized NMPC-PID consistency-deviation index is constructed. Alarm decisions are then made using an adaptive threshold and a persistent threshold-exceedance criterion. Simulation results show that, compared with conventional PID control, NMPC reduces the liquid-level root-mean-square error from 0.274 m to 0.127 m and the pressure root-mean-square error from 1.252 bar to 0.684 bar, corresponding to reductions of approximately 53.7% and 45.4%, respectively. Under valve-stuck and sensor-bias fault conditions, the constructed consistency deviation persistently exceeds the adaptive threshold and triggers an alarm. No false alarm occurs during the normal slug-flow disturbance, and the fault-detection delay is approximately 2.0 s for both fault conditions. The results indicate that the proposed method improves coordinated GLCC level-pressure control and can provide auxiliary information for identifying abnormalities in the control system.

papers.title: An Active Learning Strategy for Online Batch Fault Detection and Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Online batch fault detection and diagnosis in modern manufacturing increasingly relies on machine learning detectors trained on large volumes of labeled data. However, labeling all samples collected by high-speed, high-dimensional sensors in real time is often impractical due to limited labeling resources. Besides, most collected samples correspond to a normal production environment, resulting in a severely imbalanced class distribution. Furthermore, evolving operating conditions give rise to novel, previously unseen fault types. These constraints pose challenges for applying conventional machine learning approaches for online FDD, which typically depend on complete and balanced data sets to effectively train the fault detector. To address these constraints, a bilevel active learning framework is proposed, where a batch of samples is strategically selected at each time step to update the fault detector in real time for online FDD with limited labeling resources. At the first level, a joint exploitation-exploration sampler is developed to select a batch of samples that are highly informative for the current fault detector and likely to reveal rare or unseen fault types while explicitly minimizing the intrabatch redundancy. At the second level, a minority-aware replay sampler is designed to enhance the robustness of the query set from the first level by replacing less informative samples with more informative ones from the historical data set while maintaining the size of the query set. Finally, the resulting data set from the bilevel active learning framework is used to update the fault detector incrementally by a continual learning method. The framework is tested on synthetic data sets and real-world cases, demonstrating its superior performance compared with state-of-the-art benchmarks. History: Bianca Maria Colosimo served as the senior editor for this article. Supplemental Material: The online appendix is available at https://doi.org/10.1287/ijds.2026.0172 .

papers.title: Uncertainty in Human–Machine Shared Driving and Takeover Decision-Making
papers.abstract: In human–machine shared driving, takeover decision-making is affected by multi-source uncertainty from the environment, driver, and system. Existing studies lack integration of uncertainty modeling, evaluation, and the takeover process. This paper presents a focused review of recent literature from four aspects: uncertainty types, modeling methods, takeover decision-making process, and evaluation frameworks. It summarizes four sources of uncertainty: environment and perception, driver state, system and interaction, and situation. Modeling methods are grouped into probabilistic and Bayesian modeling, learning-based uncertainty quantification, cognitive modeling, and decision-theoretic methods. Research progress on pre-takeover risk prediction, takeover request timing, authority allocation, and trust calibration is reviewed. Current limitations include inconsistent evaluation metrics, poor cross-scenario generalization, and constraints on real-time deployment and explainability. Future work should strengthen multi-source fusion and online updating, human-adaptive takeover support, and standardized evaluation to improve the safety and timeliness of takeover decisions.

papers.title: Can World Models Generate Films? AI World Model and the Boundaries of Interactive Cinema
papers.abstract: This paper asks whether AI world models can generate films, and more specifically whether they can produce a form of interactive cinema in which viewers intervene in unfolding images. Drawing on André Bazin's account of cinema's founding desire for "a total and complete representation of reality," it situates contemporary world models such as LingBot-World, Happy Oyster, Runway's GWM-1, and Odyssey within a longer history of attempts to reproduce the world through moving images. The paper compares world models with virtual production, using the author's own AI-built lighting simulator as a case study of real-time light and shadow generation and its computational limits. It then reframes AI photography as a probabilistic mode of generation that repositions the photographer as a player exploring a space of possible outcomes rather than an author of a single fixed image. Finally, it turns to the material conditions of world models within the Anthropocene, following Kate Crawford's account of AI as an extractive industry, to argue that computing power, training data, and copyright are inseparable from questions of energy, labor, and planetary cost. The paper concludes that world models can already generate footage assembled into a finished film, but genuinely interactive cinema remains bounded by these material and infrastructural constraints.

papers.title: Bayesian optimization of exergy rate for multi-well injection schemes in carbon dioxide-based geothermal systems
papers.abstract: Carbon dioxide-based geothermal systems use captured carbon dioxide as a subsurface working fluid, coupling renewable energy production with long-term carbon dioxide utilization. Their decades-long sustainability hinges on how carbon dioxide injection rates are allocated across wells and operational stages, yet each candidate strategy demands a computationally prohibitive full-physics simulation. With the lifetime average reservoir exergy rate as the objective, Bayesian optimization is employed to make this search tractable, identifying interpretable interwell injection-rate allocations while matching the solution quality of an industry-standard optimizer at a lower computational cost. The framework is demonstrated on a geothermal reservoir with five injectors and two producers over a 30-year lifetime, comparing Uniform, Zonal, and Stepwise Injection Rate Schemes against the lifetime average reservoir exergy rate. The results demonstrate that the exergy optimization primarily navigates a fundamental trade-off between the quantity and the quality of the produced energy. Excessive injection greatly penalizes performance, reducing the lifetime average exergy rate to 429 kW at a tenfold-higher rate, below the 494 kW obtained under conservative injection, which nonetheless underutilizes the reservoir. Temporal flexibility in the injection-rate allocation resolves this tension. Relative to the Zonal Rate Scheme, the Stepwise Rate Scheme raises specific exergy by 15.6% and cuts carbon dioxide injection by 11% while still delivering a higher average exergy rate, thereby extracting more useful energy from less carbon dioxide circulation. Flow diagnostics and Proper Orthogonal Decomposition analyses further confirm the underlying mechanism. Guided by the well connectivity, optimized injection-rate allocations redirect injection spatially and temporally, extending fluid residence time, whereas the geologically anchored dominant mode of the flow field remains unchanged. This study contributes essential insights into advancing sustainable energy production techniques, and the framework is generalizable to other subsurface systems involving multiple injection and production wells.

papers.title: QUANTIFYING UNCERTAINTY IN BIOMEDICAL AND MACHINE LEARNING MODELS USING ARTIFICIAL SAMPLING AND INVERSION TECHNIQUES
papers.abstract: Modern biomedical and machine-learning problems increasingly require reliable uncertainty quantification when relevant information about the data is restricted or only partially observed, or when the inferential targets are discrete or non-numeric. In such settings, standard large-sample approximations may be difficult to apply. This dissertation develops finite-sample methods for uncertainty quantification across three problems, (i) inference for population rankings, (ii) prediction risk control in federated learning and (iii) causal hypothesis testing. First, this dissertation develops a general framework for constructing joint confidence sets for population ranks. Rank parameters are discrete and can be highly sensitive to sampling variability, particularly when populations are closely related, making standard asymptotic inference difficult. The proposed framework provides finite-sample coverage guarantees for true ranks across a broad class of statistical and machine-learning models. Its performance is studied through simulations and applications involving quantile based comparisons, Plackett--Luce models, EPL 2023 soccer team rankings, and hospital performance. Second, a framework for the control of prediction risk is proposed in federated learning, where calibration data is distributed between local servers and cannot be shared directly due to privacy or regulatory constraints. The proposed approach requires only limited information from individual servers while providing global risk control across the federated system, both in expectation and with high probability. The framework accommodates three federated data structures, (i) independent and identically distributed samples across local servers, (ii) partially exchangeable samples across servers, and (iii) settings with overlapping samples. Applications to biomedical prediction, image classification, recommendation systems, and hallucination control in large-language models demonstrate its broad applicability. Third, a Bayesian--Frequentist framework is presented for causal hypothesis testing that incorporates prior information while retaining frequentist error guarantees. The framework provides finite-sample Type I error control under the specified working models and addresses three causal hypotheses: the Fisher sharp null, the finite-population weak null, and the superpopulation average-treatment-effect null. Together, these contributions address uncertainty arising from discrete inferential targets, decentralized data, and partially observed causal outcomes, providing finite-sample guarantees tailored to each setting.

papers.title: Trustworthy multimodal biosensing in cardiovascular health: integrating uncertainty, causality, and signal integrity for clinical reliability
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) monitoring increasingly relies on multimodal biosensors, including electrocardiography (ECG), photoplethysmography (PPG), and advanced imaging systems. While deep learning has enhanced the analytical capacity of these biosensors, the translation of multimodal sensing data into clinical practice is hindered by a trustworthiness gap. Current biosensing architectures often lack robustness to sensor noise, produce poorly calibrated confidence estimates, ignore physiological causality, and fail to align with clinician workflows. Employing a systematic narrative review methodology across PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, and arXiv (2018–2026), this paper synthesizes the literature around six interconnected challenge areas in biosensor data integration: uncertainty quantification and conflict resolution; handling missing and misaligned modalities; knowledge-guided representation and fusion; causal and evidential reasoning; robust clinical evaluation; and human-centered integration. We propose a taxonomy of fusion strategies based on their trustworthiness properties and identify critical limitations in current methodologies, such as the tendency of black-box transformers to exploit spurious correlations in sensor data and the brittleness of early fusion under distribution shift. Furthermore, we outline a comprehensive research roadmap emphasizing causal disentanglement, federated multimodal learning, and interactive clinician-AI loops. By bridging algorithmic innovation with biosensor reliability, this review provides a blueprint for developing reliable, interpretable, and equitable multimodal biosensing systems. However, we emphasize that while these technical directions are promising, prospective clinical validation, standardized regulatory benchmarks, and equitable dataset curation remain essential prerequisites before these systems can be considered clinically validated solutions capable of transforming cardiovascular care.

papers.title: Oxygen partial pressure controlled lattice and electrical transport evolution of pulsed-laser-deposited RuO x films
papers.abstract: Abstract Rutile RuO 2 is a conductive oxide whose electronic properties are strongly coupled to lattice structure and oxygen stoichiometry. Here, we demonstrate that the growth oxygen partial pressure ( P O 2 ) provides an effective parameter for controlling the structural and electrical transport evolution of pulsed-laser-deposited RuO x films on α-Al 2 O 3 (0001). Within the rutile growth regime, decreasing P O 2 produces pronounced lattice expansion and systematic transport evolution associated with increasing oxygen deficiency. Two fitted XRD components in the 0.05–0.005-Pa films suggest a transitional regime. At 10 -3 Pa, the series reaches a distinct Ru-rich state showing Ru-like structural and two-carrier transport characteristics. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) further reveals strong depletion of the lattice-oxygen component, supporting a strongly Ru-rich composition with a substantial metallic-Ru contribution. These results establish a unified P O 2 -driven evolution of RuO x films and highlight the importance of distinguishing metallic-Ru contributions when evaluating the intrinsic electronic and spin-related properties of RuO 2 films.

papers.title: Forecasting Regional NEET Rates in Europe: A Spatio-Temporal Systems Analysis of Persistence, Socioeconomic Context, and Transferability
papers.abstract: Regional disparities in the share of young people not in employment, education, or training (NEET) remain an important challenge for European labour-market and social-inclusion policies. This study develops a leakage-aware spatio-temporal forecasting framework for regional NEET rates across 251 NUTS-2 regions in 30 European countries over 2005–2025. Predictive information is decomposed into temporal persistence (T), regional socioeconomic conditions (S), and external spatial context (P), and forecasting models are evaluated using expanding-window temporal validation, a locked 2022–2025 test period, unseen-region experiments, strict cold-region prediction, nested leave-one-country-out evaluation, and conformal uncertainty quantification. Under the locked future evaluation, the temporally selected ElasticNet model using T+S+P achieved the lowest observed RMSE among the evaluated models (RMSE = 1.685; R2 = 0.867), corresponding to a 9.8% improvement over naive persistence. Ablation analysis showed that regional history was the dominant source of predictive information. Socioeconomic conditions produced a larger numerical improvement beyond temporal persistence, whereas the additional reduction in error from spatial context was small and was not statistically distinguishable from zero under either region- or country-cluster bootstrap resampling. Generalisation performance depended strongly on the evaluation setting: CatBoost performed best in spatial transfer when local history was available, whereas ElasticNet was strongest when transfer to unseen regions was combined with forecasting into the future test period. Under strict cold-start conditions without focal-region NEET history, CatBoost again achieved the strongest performance. Finally, standard conformal prediction under-covered the highest-NEET observations despite strong overall coverage, while predicted-risk-based Mondrian calibration increased coverage in the >20% NEET group from 83.7% to 93.9%. The findings demonstrate that regional NEET forecastability depends not only on model choice but also on temporal persistence, information availability, validation design, and uncertainty calibration.

papers.title: Explainable AI for Acute Ischemic Stroke Neuroimaging: A Critical Review of SHAP and Grad-CAM Applications and Their Methodological Limitations
papers.abstract: In the triage of acute ischemic stroke (AIS), rapid non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT), computed tomography angiography (CTA), and diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (DWI) guide intravenous thrombolysis and endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). Machine learning and deep learning models have reported high discrimination for ischemic lesion detection, malignant cerebral edema (MCE), and 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) outcomes. However, opaque model architectures hinder clinical interpretation. Materials and Scope: This critical review is based on a structured PubMed/MEDLINE query (1 January 2021 to 15 August 2026). Among 34 candidate records, two were excluded during initial screening, and two were unretrievable, yielding 30 fully appraised primary prediction studies (24 acute-AIS core studies and six adjacent neurovascular models). Eight acute-AIS studies were prioritized for detailed main-text comparison, while the remaining 22 studies were comprehensively retained in supplementary synthesis. All 30 available models underwent dual evaluation: prediction-model risk of bias via PROBAST+AI and an independent eight-dimension XAI validity appraisal. Overall risk of bias was High in 93.3% (28/30; driven primarily by Domain 4, analysis) and Unclear in 6.7% (2/30; Li et al. and Huang H. et al.); no study was rated Low. Multicollinearity and Attribution Sensitivity: In radiomic and hemodynamic modeling, strong dependence among interdependent imaging predictors (e.g., ASPECTS, core infarct volume, Tmax > 6 s hypoperfusion volume, and white matter hyperintensities) complicates feature-level SHAP interpretation. Interventional or other marginal-reference formulations can break the dependence between observed and integrated-out features and may evaluate combinations that are poorly supported by the empirical joint distribution. Consequently, individual-feature attributions may be sensitive to the explainer formulation and background/reference distribution and should not be interpreted as unique biological or causal effects. Coarse Saliency and Modality Bias: Grad-CAM generates spatially coarse attribution maps due to convolutional downsampling, making it susceptible to skull-base CT beam-hardening artifacts and MRI susceptibility artifacts. Furthermore, unimodal Grad-CAM architectures inherently fail to contextualize non-imaging clinical covariates (e.g., baseline NIHSS, onset-to-door time). Validation-stage Discrimination and Calibration: Across multicenter studies, cross-cohort discrimination is heterogeneous rather than uniformly attenuated. Cao et al. showed marked internal-to-external attenuation (AUC 0.918 to 0.755), whereas Huang L. et al. (0.78 to 0.88) and Li et al. (0.84 to 0.86) showed preserved or improved external discrimination. Training/development, internal validation, and independent external-validation stages must be distinguished. Calibration and uncertainty quantification (UQ) require separate evaluation; explanation maps alone do not establish reliable clinical probabilities. XAI must transition from descriptive post hoc visualizations into validated clinical decision support. Safe translation requires explicit reporting and sensitivity analysis of feature-dependence handling, quantitative saliency validation (e.g., lesion-mask intersection-over-union [IoU] or Pointing Game hit rates against expert anatomical segmentations, alongside deletion/insertion fidelity curves), multi-vendor image harmonization, and uncertainty quantification. Grouped or hierarchical attribution may be considered when appropriate to the intended explanatory target.

papers.title: A geomorphic process-informed machine learning strategy for interpretable soil thickness mapping in the subtropical hilly regions of Southern China
papers.abstract: Abstract Soil thickness exhibits strong spatial heterogeneity in hilly regions, and its predictive mapping is hindered by the complexity of geomorphic processes and limited model interpretability. We develop an interpretable, process-informed framework integrating variable construction, multi-algorithm comparison, uncertainty quantification and slope-zone interpretation, and apply it in Xunwu County, subtropical China. Using 513 profiles and 35 variables spanning terrain, climate, erosion, vegetation, spectral and composite information, we compared five machine learning models—Random Forest, quantile regression forest (QRF), XGBoost, CatBoost and LightGBM—and selected the final model on held-out test data. Process information entered through process-informed features (three terrain core variables and six interaction composites) and slope-stratified interpretation and uncertainty evaluation. The composites supported interpretation, but removing them changed the mean R² from 0.418 to 0.443 (paired 95% CI − 0.015 to + 0.060), so their predictive benefit remains unproven. CatBoost achieved the highest mean R² under repeated random splits (0.418 ± 0.056; RMSE 22.94 cm; MAE 16.65 cm), followed by XGBoost (0.416 ± 0.065); the difference was not significant. This accuracy reflects local interpolation within the sampled domain: under spatial blocking and leave-quadrant-out validation, R² was − 0.84 to − 0.91 and − 0.03, respectively. The 90% QRF intervals achieved 85.4% coverage, increasing to 87.7% after conformal calibration, with a mean width of 70.4 cm. The applicability domain covered 92.9% of the area. SHAP showed that climate and topographic position dominated the gentle and transitional zones, whereas slope, spectral variables and vegetation were more prominent in the steep zone. These results support local, slope-stratified soil thickness mapping and interpretation rather than prediction in spatially independent areas.

papers.title: Numerical and hybrid physics-informed neural network study of magnetohydrodynamic blood-based Jeffrey ternary hybrid nanofluid flow over a wedge
papers.abstract: Introduction The current study explores the magnetohydrodynamic flow, heat transfer, and entropy generation characteristics of a blood-based Jeffrey ternary hybrid nanofluid containing graphene oxide (GO), titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ), and iron oxide (Fe 3 O 4 ) nanoparticles over an impermeable wedge embedded in a porous medium. The mathematical model accounts for the effects of the magnetic field, porous-medium resistance, thermal radiation, heat generation/absorption, viscous dissipation, and Jeffrey fluid rheology. Methods Through appropriate similarity transformations, the governing partial differential equations are converted into a system of nonlinear ordinary differential equations. The transformed equations are solved numerically using a boundary value problem (BVP) solver and subsequently analyzed through a Hybrid Physics-Informed Neural Network (HPINN) framework. The proposed HPINN combines governing-equation residuals, boundary constraints, and sparse numerical anchor data to obtain physically consistent predictions. The effects of the magnetic parameter, porous-medium resistance parameter, radiation parameter, Brinkman number, heat source/sink parameter, and Jeffrey fluid parameter on the velocity, temperature, entropy generation, skin-friction coefficient, and Nusselt number are examined in detail. Result The results show that the momentum transport characteristics are strongly influenced by the magnetic, porous-medium resistance, and Jeffrey fluid parameters, whereas thermal radiation enhances thermal boundary-layer growth. Entropy generation increases with increasing Brinkman number and Jeffrey fluid parameter, indicating greater thermodynamic irreversibility, particularly near the wedge surface. In addition, the HPINN predictions show close agreement with the benchmark numerical solutions and demonstrate satisfactory predictive capability for the transport quantities studied. Discussion The proposed methodology presents an efficient and reliable computational tool for the analysis of non-Newtonian hybrid nanofluid transport phenomena in biomedical engineering, thermal management systems, and intelligent heat-transfer applications.

papers.title: Robustness in foundation models
papers.abstract: Foundation models have transformed artificial intelligence (AI) by providing general-purpose representations that can be adapted to a wide range of tasks and modalities. As these models become increasingly integrated into real-world systems, robustness can no longer be viewed as a single property evaluated at deployment. Instead, robustness emerges throughout the entire lifecycle of a foundation model, from pretraining and adaptation to deployment, monitoring, and human interaction. This survey presents a unified framework for robustness in foundation models based on three complementary paradigms: a priori robustness, which shapes representations during pretraining; a posteriori robustness, which adapts and aligns models after training; and post hoc robustness, which evaluates and safeguards models during deployment. This study introduces primary and secondary robustness as complementary perspectives on the learning problem and uses them to analyze self-supervised learning, transformers, multimodal fusion, task-specific adaptation, alignment, representation editing, red teaming, explainability, and uncertainty quantification. This study further extends robustness beyond technical model properties to include socio-technical deployment factors such as accountability, fairness, privacy, human–AI interaction, and operational adoption. By organizing existing research through a lifecycle perspective, this study shows that robust foundation models arise not from a single technique, but from the interaction of learning objectives, adaptation mechanisms, transparency tools, and governance processes that collectively support reliable and trustworthy deployment.

papers.title: Final-Command Constraint Enforcement for Hybrid Learning-Predictive Vehicle Lateral Control: An Offline Audit on Real Driving Logs with Real-Time Feasibility Benchmarking
papers.abstract: Abstract Hybrid vehicle controllers that combine learned and predictive steering proposals require constraint enforcement at the final actuator command. This study presents an offline constraint-audit framework for a lateral-acceleration inner loop integrating implicit Q-learning (IQL), model predictive control (MPC), and final high-order control barrier function (HOCBF) projection. A platform-specific affine steering-response model and calibration-derived residual margin define the admissible torque interval, onto which the fused IQL–MPC command is projected. Experiments use three public vehicle archives from the commaSteeringControl dataset, comprising 899,188 observations, 756,941 eligible transitions, and 30,892 held-out states for command auditing. The response model achieved held-out acceleration root-mean-square errors of 0.02715, 0.02819, and 0.02075 m/s² for Genesis, Kia, and Toyota, respectively, with residual-envelope coverage near the nominal 95% level. Under the default configuration, final-filter projection yielded zero model-inequality violations at the audited states across all three platforms, compared with pre-filter rates of 5.20%, 7.10%, and 0.08%. Ablation and sensitivity analyses characterized the contributions of IQL, MPC, and residual calibration, while alternative regression specifications revealed instability in the fitted torque-response coefficient. Sequential testing on a desktop-class central processing unit (CPU) measured a mean pipeline latency of 3.097 ms, with no deadline misses at 100 Hz; HOCBF projection accounted for less than 1% of mean computational time. The results indicate that applying HOCBF projection after command fusion improves model-conditional constraint admissibility with limited computational overhead in the evaluated offline setting.

papers.title: UQ-SegNet: An instance segmentation method with uncertainty quantification for crystallization processes
papers.abstract: Abstract Reliable crystal detection is critical for crystallization quality control. Small, densely distributed crystals dominate crystallization images. Their blurred boundaries and low contrast make segmentation prone to missing them or merging neighboring crystals. These errors distort the crystal size distribution (CSD) obtained from the segmentation results, so segmentation reliability must also be assessed. We propose UQ-SegNet to segment individual crystals and quantify pixel-level uncertainty. A High-Frequency Fusion Multiscale Convolutional Attention module combines discrete cosine transform filtering with multiscale attention to retain small-crystal edges. A Position-Aware Head adds positional encoding to ROI features to improve crystal localization, and a Bayesian Decoder estimates epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty with Monte Carlo Dropout. UQ-SegNet achieves the highest AP75 (72.13%) and APs (61.30%) among compared models, and its CSD agrees most closely with the annotations. Both uncertainty types correlate positively with pixel errors. The method provides the CSD with pixel-level uncertainty for assessing the underlying segmentation.

papers.title: Recycling and Reuse of Metal Powders in Electron Beam Powder Bed Fusion: A Review
papers.abstract: Electron beam powder bed fusion (EB-PBF) is a vacuum-based metal additive manufacturing technique that selectively melts metal powder layers with a high-energy electron beam; it features low residual stress, high build efficiency and few support requirements, and is widely applied to near-net-shape fabrication of hard-to-machine alloys such as Ti-6Al-4V, Inconel 718 and γ-TiAl. After each build, approximately 95%–98% of the un-melted powder can be recovered, sieved and re-used, making powder recycling critical to both cost reduction and sustainable manufacturing. Focusing on literature of the past fifteen years (2011–2026) together with key earlier works, this review summarizes the recovery–reuse loop and powder characterization methods, and classifies powder degradation into chemical (oxidation and elemental evaporation at high temperature in vacuum), physical (mechanical damage, morphological deterioration and particle-size drift) and functional (loss of flowability and charging behavior) aspects. It then analyzes the effects of powder reuse on part density, microstructure, static strength, impact toughness and fatigue, fatigue performance being the most sensitive to powder state. Recycling behaviors of Ti-6Al-4V, Inconel 718, γ-TiAl, H13 steel, CoCrMo and copper powders are compared, followed by quality-control strategies such as fresh-powder blending, sieving management, in-process monitoring and standardization, and reported powder reuse limits. Remaining problems (scattered characterization approaches, lack of unified reuse criteria, insufficient in-situ monitoring) and future directions toward standardized powder-quality metrics, online monitoring and closed-loop recycling are discussed.

papers.abstract: Hydroclimatic volatility across the Mediterranean Basin increases the need for reliable river-discharge prediction, particularly in data-scarce coastal catchments where random validation and untested station representativeness may overstate skill. This study develops a Bayesian-optimization workflow for the Alata River Basin, Türkiye, using meteorological predictors and one-day lags of precipitation and air temperature. Gaussian Process Regression, Support Vector Regression, and Multi-Layer Perceptron models, together with BO-tuned variants, were evaluated using a chronological 80/20 split and time-ordered cross-validation. Station-specific datasets showed that data source and record completeness changed predictive accuracy and model ranking. At MERS, BO-MLP achieved the highest test R2 (0.889), while BO-SVR yielded the lowest MAE. At ERDM, baseline SVR performed best overall (R2 = 0.869), whereas BO-MLP and BO-GPR were the strongest optimized configurations. A three-scenario Monte Carlo experiment with 30 replications per scenario showed robust gains for SVR and MLP, while GPR improvements were smaller and condition-dependent across controlled data conditions.

papers.title: Toward Self-Regulating Oscillating Water Column Systems: State of the Art in Wave-to-Wire Control, Intelligent Adaptation, and Reliability
papers.abstract: Oscillating water column (OWC) wave energy converters operate under variable and nonlinear marine conditions, making advanced control essential for efficient, stable, and reliable energy conversion. This review examines the evolution of OWC control from conventional turbine-level regulation toward predictive, intelligent, adaptive, and fault-aware operation, with emphasis on their contribution to self-regulating systems. The literature is synthesized around three interconnected pillars—stability, performance, and reliability—covering control-oriented modeling, classical and optimal control, model predictive control, wave forecasting, learning-based methods, robust control, latching, fault diagnosis and fault-tolerant control, energy storage, grid integration, and control co-design. Representative studies are assessed according to monitored variables, required information, control actions, integration across the wave-to-wire chain, and validation maturity. The synthesis shows that building blocks for self-regulation already exist, including prediction, adaptive operating-point control, power management, health monitoring, and fault accommodation. However, these capabilities remain fragmented across system layers, objectives, and validation environments, revealing an integration gap, particularly for coordinated wave-to-wire operation under realistic conditions. Based on this evidence, a hierarchical roadmap is proposed that combines sensing and state estimation, predictive modeling, and a proposed control-oriented digital-twin layer, supervisory multi-objective control, local conversion control, fault and health management, and online adaptation.

papers.title: An Overview and Applications of Uncertainty Quantification
papers.abstract: The analysis and decision-making of scientific data and models have become increasingly important with the progress of data science, artificial intelligence, and computing. Although such analyses draw on available data, limited samples, measurement errors, missing data, and model assumptions all affect the results. In addition, many complex systems are inherently random. Therefore, in addition to prediction of a subject under study by a model, the uncertainty in the prediction must be studied. Uncertainty quantification (UQ) uses probability theory, statistics, and computational methods to study the sources of uncertainty and their magnitudes, and to study the effects of uncertainty in model results. This paper discusses sources of uncertainty in data, models, and randomness; uses confidence intervals, probability distributions, Bayesian methods, and Monte Carlo methods for UQ; and presents applications of these methods in healthcare, climate science, and artificial intelligence. UQ does not aim to make unknowns vanish; it makes model results more credible by describing the uncertainties in the results.

papers.title: AI-enabled XR digital twins for integrated electric mobility and urban energy systems: A review and conceptual co-optimization framework
papers.abstract: This review critically synthesizes research at the intersection of artificial intelligence (AI), digital twins, extended reality (XR), electric mobility, and urban energy systems, with two contributions: a structured evidence synthesis and a conceptual Integrated Mobility-Energy Digital Twin (IMED) co-optimization framework. A PRISMA-informed workflow covers Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar from January 2020 to 15 September 2026, with thematic coding of AI prediction/control, EV-grid interaction, digital-twin maturity, XR decision support, validation, and deployment barriers. IMED is positioned as a conceptual architecture rather than a validated real-time platform. Its contribution is the joint specification of mobility and electrical decision variables and constraints, distinction among digital models, digital shadows, and bidirectionally synchronized twins, and a governed XR feedback pathway enabling authorized human input to modify bounded priorities, constraints, scenario approval, annotations, or safe overrides. A multi-objective formulation addresses charging cost, emissions, congestion, travel time, battery degradation, user inconvenience, and grid risk. Key gaps include city-scale validation, benchmark datasets, interoperability, cybersecurity, uncertainty quantification, and developing-country evidence. Proposed evaluation targets include grid conflicts, renewable-energy utilization, charging cost, accessibility, emissions, reliability, latency, constraint violations, and human decision quality.
