papers.title: GSC-X Industrial Sandbox — Industrial Validation V1: Predictive Nonlinear Control, Productivity, Delay Robustness and Executive Upgrade Benchmarking
papers.abstract: GSC-X Industrial Sandbox — Industrial Validation V1 This report presents the computational validation of the GSC-X predictive executive control architecture for nonlinear industrial-process environments. The study consolidates three validation campaigns: Industrial Productivity V1 (TRUE N3000), Hard Delay Factory (TRUE N10000), and Industrial Upgrade V2 (TRUE N10000), complemented by an exploratory comparison with delay-aware nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC). Key validation findings: Industrial Productivity V1: GSC-X v9.1 achieved model-defined productivity of 2.0948 compared with 0.4247 for conventional PID control, while reducing modeled control energy from 145.3862 to 67.5430 and unsafe exposure from 57.0709 to 18.2565. Both controllers achieved survival of 1.000. Hard Delay Factory: GSC-X v9.1 maintained survival of 1.000 across the tested control delays of 10, 50, 150, and 300 ms. At 300 ms, PID survival decreased to 0.8802. Industrial Upgrade V2: In the separate CHAOS 450 ms benchmark, Upgrade V2 reduced unsafe exposure by approximately 63.3% and increased model-defined productivity by approximately 63.2% relative to GSC-X v9.1. Exploratory NMPC comparison: A later, limited experiment identified scenarios in which delay-aware NMPC achieved better energy efficiency and productivity than GSC-X Upgrade V2, reinforcing the importance of independent and appropriately matched comparisons. The results suggest that predictive executive architectures can improve selected measures of stability, productivity, and disturbance resilience within defined computational environments. Scientific scope and limitations: These findings are based on computational sandbox experiments. They do not constitute certification, experimental validation on commercial manufacturing equipment, or evidence of universal superiority over conventional control methods. Reported productivity, energy, and unsafe-exposure measures are model-defined metrics. The publication includes both English and Czech versions of Industrial Validation V1. papers.title: Corrosion and corrosion fatigue studies of PBF-EB/M-manufactured porous iron in simulated body fluid
papers.abstract: Abstract One of the biggest limitations for the use of iron in biodegradable implant material applications is its slow corrosion rate and stress shielding. This research, therefore, focuses on the potential of increasing the corrosion rate and reducing the stiffness by tailoring the porosity of the substrates. The materials were prepared using powder bed fusion-electron beam melting, which allows for a high adjustment of porosity. The corrosion behavior was revealed via electrochemical impedance spectroscopy with modified simulated body fluid as an electrolyte over an immersion time of up to 48 h. Additionally, the corrosion products were investigated with Raman spectroscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy to reveal details of the corrosion mechanism. Corrosion rates were increased with higher porosity, and a critical pore size was found to be necessary to sustain accelerated corrosion and avoid the blockage of pores with corrosion products. The fatigue studies illustrate the relevance of pores, leading to a reduced fatigue lifetime of the powder bed fusion-electron beam melting Fe samples under corrosive conditions, which can be explained by both stress concentrations at defect sites and enhanced corrosion rates.

papers.title: Research Progress on Closed-Loop Control Technology for Key Operation Stages of Combine Harvesters
papers.abstract: During the operation of a combine harvester, the crop state changes continuously and the load disturbances are obvious, while low loss, high efficiency and stability constrain each other, so it is difficult to take all of them into account by relying only on fixed parameters or single-variable open-loop regulation. This paper summarizes the perception, decision and execution mechanisms according to four types of stages, namely forward speed and feed rate, threshing and separation, cleaning, and header profiling, and compares the progress of machine learning, fuzzy control, model predictive control, multi-sensor fusion and soft measurement according to the completeness of the closed loop and the level of validation. Research is moving from single-parameter feedback toward multi-source perception, feedforward-feedback fusion and multi-variable coordinated optimization, but online quality perception, cross-crop generalization, subsystem coupling, real-time deployment and long-term field validation remain weak. Follow-up work should strengthen model-data fusion estimation, hierarchical multi-objective control, lightweight deployment, actuator dynamic compensation and safety fault tolerance, so as to improve the autonomous operation capability in complex field environments.

papers.title: An Overview of the Applicability of Artificial Intelligence Learning Techniques for Agricultural Crop Yield Prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate and timely crop yield prediction is essential for ensuring global food security, optimising agricultural resource allocation and informing policy decisions in an era of accelerating climate change. The rapid growth of satellite remote-sensing archives, high-resolution weather and soil datasets, and advances in machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have led to new approaches with promise at regional and national scales. This review examines the current state of ML and DL applications in crop yield prediction, covering classical ML; deep learning, including Transformers; transfer learning; hybrid and ensemble models; explainable AI; and uncertainty quantification. Classical ML approaches include Random Forest, XGBoost and Support Vector Machines, while deep learning architectures include CNNs, LSTMs and CNN-LSTM hybrids. Emerging Transformer-based models use self-attention to model long-range temporal dependencies, while transfer learning strategies support adaptation across regions and crop varieties. Explainable AI (XAI) techniques, including SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME), attention-based attribution and counterfactual explanations, help bridge the gap between predictive accuracy and agronomic interpretability. Uncertainty quantification methods include Bayesian neural networks, Monte Carlo dropout, quantile regression and conformal prediction. Several shortcomings remain, including the lack of standardised benchmark datasets, inconsistent evaluation practices that may inflate reported performance, and limited provision of calibrated prediction intervals. The unresolved question is not simply which algorithm achieves the highest accuracy on a given dataset, but whether these models can reliably predict yields under challenging climatic conditions. This review outlines directions for benchmarking, uncertainty-aware modelling and the integration of explainability into decision-support tools for agricultural crop yield prediction.

papers.title: A hybrid machine learning framework for accurate petrophysical prediction: application to formation resistivity in the Nubian reservoir
papers.abstract: Utilizing Machine Learning (ML) approaches to predict petrophysical parameters is becoming increasingly common due to their effectiveness in identifying non-linear relationships. Formation resistivity (RT) is a crucial petrophysical parameter that significantly impacts geophysical and geological applications; however, although ML algorithms have shown effectiveness in forecasting RT, several limitations have been identified in numerous investigations, particularly in handling the complex relationships within heterogeneous reservoirs. This study proposes two innovative hybrid ML frameworks for RT prediction using data from the Nubian reservoir in Libya. The primary hybrid model (ELM-RBF) integrates an Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) with a Radial Basis Function (RBF) network, while the secondary hybrid model (MLP-GPR) amalgamates a Multi-layer Perceptron (MLP) with a Gaussian Process Regressor (GPR). All algorithms are meticulously optimized via Grid Search Optimization (GSO). The models were evaluated against the corresponding standalone models. Prior to model development, a comprehensive data preprocessing workflow was implemented, incorporating a novel denoising process to enhance data quality. The proposed hybrid models have superior predictive accuracy and consistency compared to the Standalone models. Improved generalization performance and reduced overfitting were confirmed through multiple evaluation metrics, including the Generalization Gap (GG), Generalization Error Ratio (GER), and Normalized Root Mean Square Error (NRMSE). Ensemble-based uncertainty quantification further indicates lower predictive uncertainty and enhanced robustness of the hybrid models. Additionally, a novel empirical equation for RT prediction was developed using Gene Expression Programming (GEP), providing a reference for estimating RT in the study area and adjacent regions where implementation of hybrid models may be challenging.

papers.title: Designing High-Quality-Factor Electrospun Nanofiber Air Filters with Physics-Informed Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Abstract High filtration efficiency ($\eta$) and low pressure drop ($\Delta P$) are desirable performance parameters for an air filter, and the quality factor \rev{(QF)} is the standard figure-of-merit that balances particle capture against breathability. In this work, we present a physics-informed machine-learning framework that predicts efficiency, pressure drop, and the derived quality factor for electrospun fibrous filters. Two physics-informed neural networks \rev{(PINNs), formulated as physics-constrained networks in which the filtration laws are imposed as hard constraints rather than as differential-equation residual penalties,} are constructed: a pressure-drop network constrained by Darcy’s law and an efficiency network constrained by the classical exponential log-penetration relation. By embedding these filtration laws as differentiable constraints, the framework learns effective permeability and single-fiber efficiency, enabling physically consistent prediction and optimization of the quality factor. A dataset spanning multiple polymers, fiber diameters, packing fractions, membrane thicknesses, face velocities, and filtration particle sizes is compiled from published experimental studies. The pressure-drop PINN attains $R^2=0.982$, outperforming all five purely data-driven regressors, while the efficiency PINN attains $R^2=0.984$. Systematic variation of the input parameters identifies fiber diameter as the dominant lever for improving QF, shows that the optimal QF depends on particle size, and confirms the weak dependence of QF on membrane thickness. These results indicate that physics-guided learning offers a generalizable and physically consistent route to the predictive design of high-performance, energy-efficient electrospun filters.

papers.title: Advanced Modeling and Hybrid Manufacturing of Heat Exchangers: Design Considerations, Challenges and Opportunities
papers.abstract: Heat Exchangers (HXs) are critical components in aerospace, automotive, energy, and thermal management systems, where increasing demands for compactness, lightweight structures, and enhanced thermal efficiency are driving the development of advanced manufacturing approaches. Conventional manufacturing methods are limited in their ability to fabricate complex internal geometries, topology-optimized flow paths, and multi-material architectures required for next-generation HX designs. Additive manufacturing (AM) methods, such as Directed Energy Deposition (DED) and Powder Bed Fusion (PBF), offer significant geometric freedom and material efficiency. However, limitations related to surface roughness, dimensional accuracy, residual stress, and post-processing remain major barriers to industrial adoption. Hybrid Manufacturing (HM), which integrates additive and subtractive processes within a unified platform, has emerged as a promising solution by combining the design flexibility of AM with the precision and surface quality of conventional machining. This review examines the current state of HM technologies for advanced thermal management applications, the potential of their use for HXs, the roles of Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) architectures and Functionally Graded Materials (FGMs), and how these can enhance the thermal performance of HXs. The findings from this review, mainly based on existing results from various heat system components, indicate that HM has the potential to improve the manufacturability and performance of complex HXs by enabling near-net-shape fabrication, high-quality surface finishing, and material tailoring within a single workflow.

papers.title: AN IMPROVED FOPID-CONTROLLED HYBRID TRANSFORMER-LESS SINGLE-PHASE GRID-CONNECTED SOLAR PV INVERTER WITH REACTIVE POWER COMPENSATION AND LEAKAGE CURRENT MITIGATION
papers.abstract: This work presents a FOPID-controlled hybrid transformer-less single-phase grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) inverter designed to mitigate leakage current while enabling reactive power compensation. Conventional transformerless inverters offer high efficiency and reduced cost but suffer from leakage current issues due to the absence of galvanic isolation, leading to safety concerns and power quality degradation. To address these challenges, a hybrid inverter topology combining DC decoupling, AC decoupling, and mid-point clamping techniques is proposed to suppress common-mode voltage variations effectively. The system employs a Fractional Order Proportional-IntegralDerivative (FOPID) controller to enhance dynamic response, improve tracking accuracy, and ensure robust performance under varying operating conditions such as irradiance fluctuations and load disturbances. The proposed control strategy enables independent regulation of active and reactive power, thereby supporting grid voltage stability and power factor correction. The performance of the system is validated using MATLAB/Simulink simulations under both open-loop and closed-loop conditions. Comparative analysis with conventional model predictive control (MPC) demonstrates significant improvements in leakage current suppression, reduced total harmonic distortion (THD), faster transient response, and enhanced stability. The proposed inverter thus provides an efficient, reliable, and gridcompliant solution for modern distributed PV systems.

papers.title: TwAIns: how artificial intelligence transforms biological digital twins from cell to population, and why validation is the limiting factor
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence has changed what a biological model can be. The digital twin, a computational replica kept in step with its living original through continuous data assimilation, is now being built at every level of biological organization, from the single cell to the whole population. I argue that deep learning, transformer architectures, physics-informed neural networks, generative models, and the first biological foundation models have moved the twin from a static system of differential equations toward an adaptive, human-relevant instrument, and that this shift is the most promising route yet to replace animal experiments with New Approach Methodologies. I trace five nested scales: the cellular AI Virtual Cell, the in vitro process and organoid twin, the physics-informed organ twin, the individual Virtual Human Twin of precision medicine, and the population twin of the Exposome and virtual control groups. At each level, I ask what the twin genuinely replaces today and what remains aspiration, resisting the temptation to sell a lifetime replica of a human that no one has yet built. The twin will not earn scientific and regulatory trust on cleverness alone. It needs next-generation validation, agreed credibility standards, and lifecycle governance. That, and not more computing, is the work ahead.

papers.title: An integrated 3D-Bioprinted skin Equivalent platform for Air-Liquid interface maturation and reproducible wound induction.
papers.abstract: The development of physiologically relevant and reproducible in vitro skin models is essential for toxicological testing, disease modelling, and regenerative medicine while reducing reliance on animal experimentation in accordance with the 3Rs principle. However, current skin culture platforms often provide limited control over the air-liquid interface and do not allow standardized wound induction, resulting in substantial experimental variability. Here, we present the Insert-Based Wound Induction Device (I-WID), an integrated 3D-printed platform designed to support the maturation of bioprinted Skin Equivalents (SE) and enable controlled and reproducible wound generation. The system combines a custom culture insert for stable air-liquid interface maintenance with a complementary wound-induction tool engineered to control wound position, geometry, and depth. The platform was validated using a 3D-bioprinted SE composed of human BJ5ta fibroblasts and HaCaT keratinocytes embedded in a commercial skin bioink. Extract-based cytotoxicity assays demonstrated that the polylactic acid and photopolymerizable resin used for device fabrication did not adversely affect cell viability under the tested conditions. Constructs maintained high viability during long-term culture, while histological and immunofluorescence analyses showed epidermal stratification, keratin 10 expression, and collagen type I deposition. Compared with commercial inserts, the I-WID supported more homogeneous keratinocyte coverage and improved tissue organization. Moreover, the wound-induction tool generated well-defined lesions with greater geometric regularity and fewer residual cells within the wound area than manual biopsy punching. Overall, the I-WID provides a modular and reproducible platform for the maturation and standardized injury of 3D-bioprinted SE, supporting future applications in wound repair research, toxicological assessment, and regenerative medicine.

papers.title: 3D bioprinting of alginate-gelatin inks with lipid nanoparticles for localized drug delivery in glioblastoma therapy.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) management is severely limited by systemic barriers, including poor blood-brain barrier penetration and off-target toxicities. Localized delivery platforms offer a promising alternative by providing prolonged therapeutic concentrations directly at the tumor site post-resection. In this study, 3D-printed scaffolds composed of sodium alginate (SA) and gelatin (GEL) inks loaded with lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) were developed as a platform for local delivery of nucleic acid molecules (siRNA fluorescent). To optimize printability and structural stability, 2 % SA (w/v) and 10 % GEL (w/v) solutions in PBS buffer (pH 7.4) were mixed at different volume ratios, including 1:1, 2:1, 5:1, and 1:5. The 2:1 SA:GEL ratio produced the most stable and well-defined printed structures. Three LNPs incorporation strategies were also evaluated, and pre-incorporation of LNPs into the SA solution resulted in the most homogeneous and stable scaffolds. Rheological analysis confirmed the ink's suitability for extrusion-based bioprinting, demonstrating pseudoplastic, shear-thinning behavior and a 55 % recovery rate essential for structural integrity. Printed scaffolds were fabricated at 13 % and 35 % infill densities and characterized by morphology, rheological behavior, release profiles, and uptake in U87 human glioblastoma cells. In vitro siRNA-LNPs release from the selected ink was architecture-dependent, reaching completion within 24 h at 35 % infill and within 8 h at 13 % infill. Furthermore, the scaffold-integrated LNPs system enabled efficient delivery of fluorescently labelled siRNA to U87 cell. These findings validate the potential of SA-GEL scaffolds as biocompatible platforms for the controlled administration of siRNA-loaded LNPs.

papers.title: LoRN: Low-Rank Noise Steering for Generative Robot Policies
papers.abstract: Noise steering improves pretrained generative robot policies by learning to select their initial noise without updating model weights. We find that actions in the evaluated world-action models are more sensitive to video noise than action noise, making video noise an expressive input for steering. However, the noise-steering methods we evaluate, in their published forms, struggle to scale to the high-dimensional noise inputs of large policy classes such as world-action models. We introduce Low-Rank Noise Steering (LoRN), a reinforcement learning method that scales noise steering to world-action models. A small steering actor selects a direction through a fixed low-rank random projection, while our norm-controlled construction keeps the resulting noise near the typical scale of a Gaussian sample. This separates the actor's control dimension from the full noise dimension, enabling steering of both video and action inputs. Across three world-action models and ten model-task pairs, video steering improves average success by 26.2 percentage points over the base policy, compared with 7.1 points for DSRL action steering. For smaller action policies, the same construction achieves comparable final success while generally improving early-training success. Steering actors trained in simulation also transfer to three physical bimanual manipulation tasks across two base policies, without additional real-world training.

papers.title: How Uncertain Is My Action? Self-Correcting Visual Planning with Frozen World Models
papers.abstract: A frozen latent world model combined with sampling-based model predictive control is a visual planner. At deployment, the executed action can depart from the commanded one, and the frozen model has no way to notice. We show that the model can be run in reverse: for any hypothesized actuation shift, it predicts what it should have observed under that shift, and comparing this prediction with what was actually observed quantifies the shift and lets the planner correct itself. Unlike the residual energy, which mixes the shift with the model's own error, the score keeps only the part of the residual that a shift can produce. This shift score detects the shift with a locally optimal test, estimates it with Cramer-Rao error bars, names the dominant generator, and compensates the planner once an alarm fires. On PushT, TwoRoom and OGBench-Cube with a frozen latent world model, measured detection follows the prediction to within 0.05 AUROC. Self-correction raises success from 0.650 to 0.862 on PushT and from 0.378 to 0.432 on the harder Cube task, levels with an oracle that is told the true shift at the same block, better than five common test-time adaptation methods. On a real robotic arm, the score identifies a base-joint offset that no joint encoder registers and reduces the reach error from 36 mm to 3-5 mm, and under shifts drawn at random and sealed before the session, estimates recover 92-94% of the error reduction achieved with the true shift. The broader implication is that a frozen world model can act as a filter by predicting the future, testing action-interface uncertainty and validity, and finally correcting failures.

papers.title: JEPA as a Transferable Optimizer: Learning and Understanding Black-Box Optimization from Reward-Agnostic Pretraining
papers.abstract: Black-box optimization evaluates candidates through simulations, rollouts, or experiments, often without gradients. Learned optimizers are usually judged by whether they outperform existing methods. We ask a complementary question: what information does a learned optimizer use from its search history? We introduce JEPA-PS (JEPA Policy Search), based on a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture. It is pretrained on random rollouts using parameter vectors and scalar returns. Its latent-prediction objective predicts the next point in an optimization trajectory rather than its reward or gradient, allowing us to examine what was tried and how well it performed. At test time, JEPA-PS reads a short evaluation history and proposes a candidate in one forward pass, without task descriptions, reward shaping, or test-time gradients. We evaluate it on 15 control environments against 12 optimizers, including evolutionary methods, Bayesian optimization, CMA-ES, and an LLM optimizer. JEPA-PS is competitive with tuned classical baselines and outperforms the LLM optimizer by more than 2x on Swimmer at 71x lower per-step cost. It also transfers zero-shot to environments excluded from pretraining. Null-model comparisons and decoder-training ablations indicate that its latent representation carries information beyond simple history statistics; every trained decoder variant performs worse than the default frozen representation. Our main finding is that the history JEPA-PS uses depends on the task. On smooth landscapes it uses the full trajectory, whereas on rugged landscapes the best-seen point carries nearly all the signal. This memory requirement has a weak positive correlation with fitness-distance correlation (FDC; r=0.112, n=7), while an independent reward-ordering sensitivity probe does not corroborate the relationship (r=-0.024, n=7). papers.title: Machine-learned acceleration of earthquake sequence simulations
papers.abstract: Earthquake sequence simulations involve slow interseismic processes and rapid dynamic ruptures. During interseismic periods, a numerical solver can take large time steps efficiently. During seismic periods, in contrast, the solver must drastically reduce the time step, and elastodynamic wave-mediated memory effects become significant; long-term simulations are therefore computationally expensive. We investigate the use of neural operators to accelerate earthquake sequence simulations. We train a Fourier neural operator (FNO) on data from high-fidelity, fully dynamic simulations to learn a jump map that advances the system state from before a seismic rupture to after it. We propose a hybrid modeling framework in which a conventional quasi-dynamic solver simulates the slow interseismic evolution, and the trained FNO replaces the solver during the computationally intensive seismic periods with wave-mediated inertial effects. The hybrid model reproduces key long-term statistics of fully dynamic simulations, including distributions of event magnitudes and recurrence times. Furthermore, it provides a much better approximation to the fully dynamic simulations than the commonly used quasi-dynamic approximation at a reduced computational expense.

papers.title: Learning and Control in Physically Coupled Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: We introduce TAG (Testbed for Autonomous Games), a compact, low-cost robotic platform for studying learning and control in physically coupled dynamical systems. TAG combines an actively tilted and steered ball-in-maze board with a top-mounted rotary inverted pendulum. The pendulum's reaction torque and vibration disturb the board and marble, while the board's tilt, driven by the maze-solving policy, simultaneously disturbs the pendulum's balance. The main challenge in learning control policies for each subsystem is accounting for the impact of one subsystem's dynamics on the other's learning process. To address this challenge, we present complementary reinforcement learning paradigms, leveraging model-based and model-free approaches to learn the control policies for the maze and pendulum, respectively. Our key finding is that introducing the pendulum causes an immediate, sharp drop in the maze policy's success rate, but the policy adapts online and recovers to its pre-coupling performance within a small number of learning episodes. Experimental results show that both policies, trained independently, successfully control the maze board and the pendulum despite their physical coupling.

papers.title: PhysDial: Adapting Pretrained Video Models for PDE Simulation under Changing Physical Conditions
papers.abstract: Simulating how physical systems respond to changing conditions is central to control, design, and scenario studies. To our knowledge, prior PDE foundation models have not been trained or evaluated on changes within trajectories. Our counterfactual test measures how far predictions move toward a changed solver branch from the same state. Models trained on fixed conditions follow changes only partly. A PDE foundation model given a condition input after pretraining barely responds. PhysDial adapts a pretrained video diffusion transformer to eight two-dimensional PDE families. Coefficients enter with the noise level, condition fields as reference frames, and equation text as a prompt. In Kolmogorov flow, switches within trajectories account for about 5% of the training samples. At matched compute, they halve the error after a change in forcing wavenumber or amplitude. A few trajectories at new amplitudes more than halve extrapolation error. Without physics pretraining, PhysDial matches or exceeds PDE foundation models under training conditions on two turbulent flows. At step 64 on the Kolmogorov test split, PhysDial has 1.07 times the solver's small-scale energy and Walrus 7.1 times. Our experiments suggest that a learned simulator uses a condition only as far as its training data make that condition necessary for prediction. Learning from trajectories that diverge under intervention can help scientific simulators predict what would happen if a system's forcing or parameters changed.

papers.title: Conformally Calibrated Adaptive Computation in Neural Operators
papers.abstract: Selecting less computation in a neural operator need not reduce inference time. We study this gap using conformal calibration to choose Fourier modes or channel width per input subject to a fixed error budget. A triangle-inequality envelope bounds all candidates simultaneously; a direct-score rule handles non-monotone candidate errors and, with an input-independent score, calibrates a static baseline under the same marginal guarantee. Under frozen-model and exchangeability assumptions, both rules bound the probability of issuing a prediction outside the budget and abstain when calibration is infeasible. On Burgers and Darcy flow across three training seeds, mode selection reduces active spectral support without a measurable latency reduction, because full-grid transforms and channel mixing dominate the cost. Narrowing channels does reduce Darcy forward cost, but reference-based selection must first compute the dense prediction. An input-only binary width selector avoids that pass and runs at 0.52-0.95 times dense latency; yet static widths calibrated under the same rule are often as fast or faster, and on a separately generated 1,000-example test set they generally achieve higher coverage, while the selector falls below its 90% target in more than half of the settings. Adaptive computation in neural operators should therefore be judged by achieved coverage and complete runtime against a matched static comparator.

papers.title: AUTOMOTIVE CONNECTING ROD
papers.abstract: The connecting rod links the piston to the crankshaft and converts the reciprocating motion of the piston into the rotary motion of the crank. In every engine cycle it is compressed by the gas force during combustion and pulled in tension by the inertia of the piston assembly near the top of the exhaust stroke, so it works under a fully alternating load at high frequency. A connecting rod failure usually destroys the engine block and crankshaft, and therefore the rod must be strong, stiff against buckling and resistant to fatigue. Because it is a reciprocating part, its mass also directly affects the inertia forces, the bearing loads and the balance of the engine. This paper presents the design and finite element analysis of a connecting rod for a single-cylinder four-stroke petrol engine of 150 cc displacement with a bore of 57 mm and a stroke of 58.6 mm. The rod was sized by the standard I-section design procedure and modelled in SolidWorks with a centre distance of 112 mm. The model was analysed in ANSYS Workbench for a compressive gas load of 8.93 kN, corresponding to a peak cylinder pressure of 3.5 MPa, and a tensile inertia load of 4.2 kN at a maximum speed of 9,000 rpm. Static structural, linear buckling, modal and fatigue analyses were carried out. Four materials were compared using the same geometry, mesh and loads: structural steel, forged alloy steel AISI 4340, aluminium alloy 7075-T6 and titanium alloy Ti6Al-4V. Under the compressive load the maximum von Mises stress was between 166.4 and 168.9 MPa for all materials and occurred at the junction of the shank and the small end. The factor of safety on yield was 1.49 for structural steel, 4.20 for AISI 4340, 3.02 for aluminium 7075-T6 and 5.25 for Ti-6Al-4V. The fatigue analysis showed that structural steel and aluminium 7075-T6 could not reach the target life of one million cycles under the alternating load, while AISI 4340 and Ti-6Al-4V could. Considering strength, fatigue life, buckling margin, manufacturability and cost, forged AISI 4340 was selected, and its I-section was then refined by thinning the web from 4.0 mm to 3.2 mm and tapering the flanges towards the small end. The refined rod has a mass of 0.282 kg against 0.312 kg for the original section, a reduction of 9.6 percent, with a maximum stress of 186.4 MPa, a factor of safety of 3.81, a buckling load factor of 24.1 and a fatigue safety factor of 1.68. Its first natural frequency is well above the crankshaft speed and its second harmonic. The work demonstrates that a computer-aided design and finite element approach can identify the critical regions of a connecting rod, compare candidate materials on a common basis and guide a weight reduction without compromising safety. The approach shortens the design cycle compared with repeated prototype forging and fatigue testing, and it provides a clear record of the reasoning behind the final material and section choice.

papers.title: AUTOMOTIVE SUSPENSION CONTROL ARM
papers.abstract: The lower control arm is one of the most heavily loaded members of a passenger car suspension. It connects the wheel knuckle to the vehicle body through a ball joint at the outer end and two rubber bushings at the inner end, and it carries the longitudinal, lateral and part of the vertical forces generated at the tyre contact patch during braking, cornering and travel over uneven roads. A failure of this component leads to a sudden loss of wheel control, so its strength, stiffness and fatigue behaviour must be established with care before it is manufactured. At the same time, the arm is part of the unsprung mass of the vehicle, and any reduction in its weight improves ride comfort, road holding and fuel economy. This work presents the design and analysis of a front lower control arm for a MacPherson strut suspension of a compact passenger car with a kerb mass of about 1,200 kg. The geometry of the arm was modelled in SolidWorks using hard points taken from a typical front suspension layout, and the model was transferred to ANSYS Workbench for static structural, modal and fatigue analysis. Three load cases were studied, namely braking, cornering and a combined pothole event, and the combined pothole case with 6.5 kN longitudinal, 5.8 kN lateral and 3.5 kN vertical force at the ball joint was found to govern the design. Five candidate materials were compared under identical geometry, mesh and boundary conditions: structural steel, forged alloy steel AISI 4340, aluminium alloy 6061-T6, aluminium alloy 7075-T6 and titanium alloy Ti-6Al-4V. For each material the equivalent von Mises stress, total deformation, factor of safety based on yield strength, mass and first natural frequency were recorded. Structural steel reached a maximum stress of 186.4 MPa with a factor of safety of only 1.34, while aluminium 7075-T6 reached 182.9 MPa with a factor of safety of 2.75 at a mass of 1.22 kg against 3.42 kg for the steel arm. Based on this comparison, aluminium alloy 7075-T6 was selected, and the arm was refined by adding lightening pockets in the web and a stiffening rib along the inner edge, guided by the low-stress regions seen in the contour plots. The refined arm has a mass of 1.08 kg, a maximum von Mises stress of 211.6 MPa near the front bushing neck, a total deformation of 1.94 mm and a factor of safety of 2.38. This represents a mass reduction of 68.4 percent compared with the structural steel baseline.

papers.title: Enriched Proximal Gradient Descent Deep Unfolding Framework for Rice Leaf Disease Classification
papers.abstract: Rice leaf diseases create a critical threat to global food security, which requires rapid and effective diagnostic solutions.Existing Deep Learning (DL) frameworks, such as Residual Network (ResNet) and Visual Geometry Group Network (VGGNet) struggle to handle variations in lighting, background canopy clutter, and visual metamerism, which reduces the detection performance under various environmental conditions.To address these challenges, this research introduces the Enriched Proximal Gradient Descent Deep Unfolding Framework (EPGD-DUF) to develop an environmentally robust model to reduce sensitivity towards domain-specific illumination and background variations for rice-leaf disease detection.EPGD-DUF architecture employs the Proximal Gradient Descent (PGD) algorithm across four parameter-shared stages to mathematically model software-synthesized pseudo-spectral latent reconstruction.This integrates a Cross-Channel Latent Fusion Module (CCLFM) to suppress soil-line vectors and applies a Hyperspherical ArcFace classification head to strictly separate angular classes.The detection performance of the EPGD-DUF is evaluated on two standard datasets, achieving 99.83% accuracy on the laboratorycontrolled Mendeley rice leaf disease dataset and 98.89% accuracy on the highly cluttered Paddy Doctor field dataset.The proposed EPGD-DUF achieves higher accuracy than other baseline models, such as ResNet50, VGG16, ConvNeXt, and Vanilla PINN baselines under the corresponding dataset specific evaluation protocols.Under an explicit laboratory-to-field transfer protocol over the four classes common to both repositories, the framework retains 96.2% accuracy on the held-out target-domain test set, while target-domain labels were not used during adaptation or model selection, corresponding to a domain gap of 3.6 percentage points, compared with 6.0 percentage points for the strongest convolutional baseline.

papers.title: From dynamic modelling of an experimental Reversible Organic Rankine Cycle towards a digital twin—Validation and remaining challenges
papers.abstract: Reversible Organic Rankine Cycle (rORC) systems alternate between high-temperature heat pump (HTHP) and power-generation operation. In geothermal plants, they can cover peak heat demand and convert surplus heat into electricity. Frequent load changes, mode transitions, their optimisation and development of advanced control methods require detailed dynamic models, which are not yet available for rORC systems. This work presents the first such model, to the authors’ knowledge, validated experimentally in both modes of a reversible HTHP/ORC test rig. The model is developed in APROS, extended by Python-based sub-models and fitted to experimental data. The ORC net electric thermal efficiency is reproduced with a mean absolute error (MAE) of at most 0.32 percentage points, the control-relevant district heating supply temperature in HTHP mode with an MAE lower than 1 K and the mechanical coefficient of performance with an MAE of 0.31 to 0.44, demonstrating that the model captures the stationary and dynamic behaviour of the test rig in both operating modes. However, absolute HTHP predictions remain limited by a systematic overprediction of the refrigerant mass flow, partly attributed to unmodelled lubricating oil. Within these limits, the validated model provides a basis for control-oriented simulation and the development of advanced control strategies. A continuous bidirectional data exchange with the test rig remains as last step towards a digital twin.

papers.title: A conceptual framework for evaluating neural networks as instruments of scientific discovery
papers.abstract: Neural networks are increasingly used not only for prediction, but also as instruments for simulation, inverse modeling, operator learning, representation learning, and hypothesis generation. This perspective argues that their scientific value cannot be assessed by predictive accuracy alone. Architectures such as physics-informed neural networks, neural operators, graph and equivariant models, Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, long-sequence models, and foundation models for science illustrate a broader transition from data-driven fitting toward computational systems that interact with theory, experiment, and domain constraints. However, this transition also exposes methodological risks: data leakage, weak external validation, poor uncertainty quantification, limited interpretability, reproducibility gaps, and overconfidence under distribution shift. To address these issues, this article proposes the Scientific Consistency and Interpretability Framework for Neural Networks (SCI-NN), a conceptual appraisal framework for scientific neural networks based on eight dimensions: accuracy, scientific consistency, generalization, interpretability, uncertainty, computational efficiency, reproducibility, and scientific utility. Its primary use is qualitative, claim-centered appraisal; optional ordinal descriptors summarize the reported evidence without producing an overall ranking. The literature and worked examples are illustrative rather than systematic or validating. SCI-NN does not certify model validity, and its reliability and added value require empirical evaluation.

papers.title: Early In-ovo Sexing of Mojosari Duck Eggs on Day 5 Using Hybrid Feature Fusion and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Early in-ovo sexing can support more efficient hatchery management by enabling sex determination before hatching.This study investigates a non-invasive framework for sexing Mojosari duck eggs at day 5 by integrating external morphological, embryonic vascular, and Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM)-based textural features.External morphological measurements, including egg length and width, were obtained directly using a digital caliper, while egg weight was measured using a digital weighing scale; embryonic vascular and textural features were extracted from RGB candling images acquired with the eggshell intact.A total of 503 labeled eggs were analyzed.Statistical differences between female and male eggs were assessed using Welch's t-test with Holm adjustment and Hedges' g effect sizes, showing significant differences in Length, Width, Weight, and Sinus Terminalis Area.Four classifiers Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM-RBF, and XGBoost, were evaluated using Bayesian optimization and stratified cross-validation, with model configuration determined exclusively from training and validation data.On the independent test set of 100 eggs, Random Forest achieved 85.00% accuracy, 82.16% balanced accuracy, 83.41% Macro-F1, and 0.9285 ROC-AUC.Batch-held-out evaluation yielded 80.44% accuracy, 75.92% balanced accuracy, 77.22% Macro-F1, and 0.8795 ROC-AUC.The study provides application-level evidence for day-5 in-ovo sexing of Mojosari duck eggs using low-cost RGB candling, while characterizing sex-related features and contribution of feature groups (hybrid feature fusion).Future studies should validate the approach across broader duck populations, incubation stages, and imaging conditions.

papers.title: Integrated Centrifugal Pump Design Using 3D Modelling, Digital Twins, and Additive Prototyping
papers.abstract: Centrifugal pump development still moves through separate islands of information: a one-dimensional sizing calculation, a manually built solid model, a physical prototype, and a drawing package produced after the geometry is frozen.This paper proposes and tests a design technology in which parametric 3D geometry, multi-fidelity CFD, a reduced-order digital twin, additively manufactured prototypes and machine-readable documentation are all views of one versioned design record.Thirty-four continuous variables plus one discrete blade number Z (35 optimisation variables in total) control the meridional channel and the blade loading, with manufacturability enforced inside the generator; a co-Kriging surrogate coupling coarse steady and fine transient cavitating simulations drives an NSGA-III search; a POD-Galerkin model corrected by an unscented Kalman filter forms the operational twin; and the sensitivity matrix produced by the optimiser is reused to allocate manufacturing tolerances.The framework was applied to three pumps of different duty (Case A, nq = 37.0; Case B, nq = 12.7; Case C, nq = 32.3;recalculated from Eq. ( 1) with Q in m³ s⁻¹) and validated against ISO 9906 Grade 1B tests.Three results are central.First, the two-level surrogate reached the same Pareto front quality as single-fidelity Kriging with 4.2 times fewer high-fidelity simulations, and measured best-point efficiency rose by 2.9-4.7 percentage points.Second, an equivalent-sand-roughness correction brought as-built selective laser melted prototypes to within 0.9 percentage points of cast production efficiency, against an uncorrected deficit of about 5 points, which turns a printed impeller into a quantitative performance predictor rather than a form-and-fit check.Third, in a two-unit field study over 4300 h the twin tracked head to 1.2 % mean absolute error and estimated wear-ring clearance to within 0.03 mm of the post-overhaul measurement.Design-cycle and documentation metrics from 14 releases are reported as associations rather than causal effects, since the comparison was not randomised.

papers.title: Embodied Intelligent Digital Twin for autonomous operations: concept and implementation guidelines
papers.abstract: To support autonomous equipment operations in complex and dynamic scenarios, this paper proposes the concept of an Embodied Intelligent Digital Twin (EIDT) and its implementation guidelines. By adapting and integrating digital twin (DT) technology with a domain-specific foundation model (DSFM), the EIDT links physical entities’ mechanistic characteristics and dynamic states with operational domain knowledge, establishing a task cognition and autonomous operation mechanism jointly driven by mechanism, data, and knowledge. In addition, the EIDT integrates information about Operation Tasks, Operation Performers, Operation Environments, and Operation Targets to support dynamic perception, task understanding, and adaptive decision-making. A unified EIDT representation paradigm comprising a mechanistic model unit (MU), a data model unit (DU), a DSFM, and an interaction interface (I) is proposed, together with an integrated construction solution. Implementation routes are developed for task-driven autonomous operation, adaptation across tasks and scenarios, and continuous evolution across lifecycle stages. Human-robot collaborative assembly of a rotary vector (RV) reducer is used to demonstrate EIDT construction, collaborative work-system formation, autonomous operation, and application extension for collaborative manufacturing tasks. The proposed EIDT provides a theoretical framework and implementation guidelines for integrating foundation models with DTs to support perception, planning, decision-making, and execution in dynamic operational scenarios.

papers.title: Conformal Prediction for Interpretable Uncertainty in High-Stakes Decision Making
papers.abstract: Deep networks used in medicine, finance and autonomous systems report confidence scores that are often miscalibrated and that carry no guarantee once the data depart from the training distribution. Conformal prediction replaces the single score with a set of candidate outcomes and attaches a finite-sample guarantee to it. Under exchangeability, the set contains the true outcome with probability at least 1 − α, for any model and any data distribution. This article reviews the method as a tool for high-stakes decisions. It sets out the split conformal procedure and its coverage bounds, computes how the guarantee behaves at the calibration sizes available in clinical and safety-critical settings, and surveys the nonconformity scores used for classification and regression. It then examines three points at which the basic guarantee falls short in practice, namely conditional coverage across patients or subgroups, distribution shift, and losses other than miscoverage, and reviews the extensions that address each. Applications in medical imaging, pathology and language generation are assessed with the evidence on human use of prediction sets. The article closes with a proposed reporting protocol that ties the choice of α, the calibration data and the behaviour of set size to the decision the set is meant to support. The protocol has not been applied to a deployed system and is offered for testing.

papers.title: Characterizing the cognitive, social, and affective behaviors of student groups in a real-world problem-solving classroom
papers.abstract: Instructors of introductory physics courses have increasingly adopted student-centered instruction, or “active learning,” over the past few decades. Active learning is generally considered more effective because knowledge construction and learning are socially situated, and active learning strategies emphasize student interaction. Extensive literature also shows that how students interact in an active learning class, as well as the class structure itself, may significantly affect learning and performance. We recently developed an instructional method based on deliberate practice in solving “real-world” physics problems—context-rich problems that often require students to seek out information and make their own simplifying assumptions. This method drastically changes the nature of the tasks students work on during class. We therefore sought to understand how students interacted in this environment and how those interactions might relate to learning and academic performance. Data were collected from three student groups during the Spring 2022 semester at a large research university. Using a three-dimensional framework to analyze group interactions, we found substantial variation in the groups’ cognitive, social, and affective behaviors. Results showed that each group had unique strengths and self-organization strategies. However, despite sometimes responding to the material with negative emotions, typically frustration, all three groups demonstrated psychological safety and social cohesion, even when cognitive work was distributed unevenly. Future work should examine how psychological safety develops amid mutual frustration during group problem-solving.

papers.title: Enhanced Power-quality Regulation in PV-integrated Systems Using Adaptive Reduced-set Horizon-2 FCS-MPC Systems
papers.abstract: The increasing use of renewable generation and power-electronic loads makes simultaneous voltage and current power-quality regulation important in distribution systems.Unified Power Quality Conditioners (UPQCs) can address both disturbance types, but conventional control and full finite-state predictive searches may face tracking and computational trade-offs under changing operating conditions.This study presents an Adaptive Reduced-Set Horizon-2 Finite-Control-Set Model Predictive Control (RS-H2 FCS-MPC) strategy for a matrix-converter UPQC integrated with photovoltaic distributed generation (PV-DG).The controller combines 27-state discrete matrix conversion, reduced second-step prediction, adaptive magnitude restoration, switching-transition and common-mode-voltage penalties, PV power feedforward, positive-sequence synchronization, and a clean-grid deadband.Evaluation uses SEED-PQD-v1 containing 17 power-quality classes and 17,000 signals, with 100 signals reserved for parameter tuning and the remaining 16,900 used for held-out evaluation.Under Protocol A, the six-condition held-out composite evaluation profile comprising Pure Sinusoidal, Sag, Swell, Harmonics, Sag with Harmonics, and Swell with Harmonics conditions, the proposed controller obtains 0.5487% voltage total harmonic distortion (THD), 0.8149% current THD, a power factor of 0.9508, and a power-quality index of 3.9362.The full 17-class assessment is reported separately.Clean-grid operation produces zero series injection and 0% voltage THD.Paired Wilcoxon tests with Holm correction on a 25-trial matched subset support the reported controller differences within the selected disturbance conditions.The results support reduced-set predictive control for compensation under the evaluated balanced multi-disturbance conditions, while the interruption case remains energy-limited without storage.

papers.title: Reinforcement learning-based autonomous multimodel weight allocation framework for rotating machinery fault diagnosis
papers.abstract: Abstract Adaptive multimodel fusion under complex operating conditions and imbalanced data distributions remains a challenging problem in rotating machinery fault diagnosis, where model reliability varies significantly across samples and operating conditions, making fixed or heuristic fusion strategies suboptimal. To address this issue, this paper proposes a reinforcement learning-based autonomous multimodel weight allocation framework (RL-AMWF), which formulates multimodel fusion as a sample-dependent stochastic decision-making problem under uncertainty. Unlike conventional ensemble methods that rely on static or manually designed weighting rules, the proposed framework learns a policy that dynamically allocates model contributions according to uncertainty-aware observations, enabling adaptive fusion under varying diagnostic conditions. A unified state representation is constructed by integrating feature semantics, predictive distributions, and uncertainty cues, while a stochastic policy is learned to output adaptive fusion weights. A composite reward function is further designed to resolve the trade-off between overall diagnostic accuracy, weak-class sensitivity, and allocation stability, enabling non-decomposable optimization of fusion behavior. Extensive experiments on public bearing and gear datasets as well as an industrial simulation dataset demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms several baseline methods in terms of overall accuracy, macro-averaged recall, and weak-class recall. Moreover, the proposed framework exhibits superior robustness under cross-condition and noise perturbation scenarios, validating the effectiveness of reinforcement learning for uncertainty-aware multimodel fusion.

papers.title: Neural Network Approximation of Constrained Optimization for Robotic Systems
papers.abstract: Numerical optimization in real time has proven to be a reliable and essential tool for applications such as energy consumption and production optimization, path planning in autonomous driving, model predictive control (MPC), motion planning for legged robots, constrained inverse kinematics (IKs), and traffic engineering. However, the high computational demands of numerical optimization methods often result in increased costs or delays that compromise efficiency and, in some cases, feasibility. To address these challenges, research efforts have focused on making numerical optimization algorithms more computationally efficient and less resource-intensive by leveraging suboptimal solutions, exploiting problem structure, and/or approximating solutions using artificial neural networks (ANNs). In particular, neural networks have demonstrated considerable success in solving MPC problems and continuous optimization problems, especially those involving inequality constraints. In this article, we establish sufficient conditions under which a neural network can approximate the solutions to a family of general continuous optimization problems with equality and inequality constraints. We also demonstrate how these conditions can be leveraged to streamline the data collection process, reducing the effort required to generate training datasets. To the best of our knowledge, this constitutes the most general approach of its kind in the literature. As a practical demonstration, we present a shared-load drone experiment to illustrate the use of neural networks for approximating the solutions of two optimization problems: one that computes the system's IKs and another that approximates the MPC solution in a soft real-time setting.

papers.title: Distortion Behavior of Ti6Al4V and Inconel 718 LPBF Cantilever Specimens: Effects of Scan Strategy and Stress-Relief Heat Treatment
papers.abstract: Residual stresses and the resulting distortion remain major challenges in achieving high dimensional accuracy in laser beam powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) components. This study experimentally investigates the distortion behavior of PBF-LB cantilever specimens fabricated from IN718 and Ti6Al4V, with particular emphasis on the effects of scan strategy and stress-relief heat treatment. Three hatch rotation angles (31°, 45°, and 90°) were evaluated under as-built (AB) and stress-relieved conditions using 3D optical scanning measurements obtained before and after wire electrical discharge machining (EDM) separation. The AB specimens exhibited progressive deformation along the cantilever length, with Ti6Al4V developing approximately twice the distortion measured for IN718. The 90° hatch strategy produced the highest distortion, whereas 31° and 45° strategies resulted in lower deformation levels. Stress-relief heat treatment proved to be the dominant factor, reducing distortion by 94–97% and substantially decreasing the influence of hatch rotation.

papers.title: Aggregative Game-Driven Neurodynamic Approach for Hierarchical Stringent Multiple Manipulators Fuzzy Control
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a class of multiple redundant manipulators collaborative operation with comprehensive constraint tasks from the perspective of aggregative game, and the aggregated information in the game model is not accessible to the participants (players). We incorporate each participant’s estimation of the aggregated information to guide the creation of the algorithm. Since each manipulator only transmits the aggregated kinematic information, this aggregative game model reduces the communication cost of multiple manipulators network. The proposed neurodynamic algorithm is capable of handling tasks such as trajectory tracking, obstacle avoidance and posture maintenance, and can also optimize the rarely-discussed self-adjustment. In view of the unknowability of the kinematics of the manipulator, we introduce a neural operator based on fuzzy association rules to approximate the error. The convergence of the neurodynamic algorithm for generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) is provable, and it can achieve distributed optimal control of the multiple manipulators.

papers.title: A physics-informed neural network for predicting fatigue life of asphalt mixtures using the superpave indirect tensile test
papers.abstract: Durability is crucial for asphalt pavement design, which necessitates an accurate prediction of the fatigue life of asphalt mixtures under complex environmental and loading conditions. A prevailing fatigue life prediction method, developed based on Hot Mix Asphalt fracture mechanics (HMA-FM), relies on a healing curve to characterise fatigue-healing properties that are highly sensitive to environmental factors. This study extends the HMA-FM framework by integrating a physics-informed neural network (PINN) to model the nonlinear dependencies of Indirect Tensile (IDT) test parameters on environmental factors. A novel PINN fatigue-healing (PINN-FH) model is proposed to predict the fatigue life of IDT samples. The key dataset for training and validating the PINN-FH model was quantified via Superpave IDT tests that control dynamic water exposure, aging duration, and temperature. Results demonstrate that the PINN-FH model accurately captures environmental effects on IDT fatigue life. Cross-dataset validation confirms the PINN-FH model’s generalisability.

papers.title: Tech-Infused Learning: ICT-Enhanced Problem-Based Learning for Critical Thinking Skills Improvement
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the effectiveness of Information and Communication Technology (ICT)-enhanced Problem-Based Learning (PBL) in improving the critical thinking skills of Grade 12 Technical-Vocational-Livelihood (TVL)–Home Economics students at Perez National High School. It provided practical training in workplace safety practices through immersive simulations designed to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and real-world applications. Specifically, the study addressed students' limited understanding of workplace safety practices to help mitigate the risks associated with unsafe workplace behaviors. The study employed a quasi-experimental research design and used criterion sampling, a purposive sampling technique, to select 40 students who were divided into two groups: 20 students in the control group, who received traditional instruction, and 20 students in the experimental group, who were taught using ICT-enhanced PBL. A 30-item multiple-choice test was administered to assess students' critical thinking skills before and after the intervention. The data were analyzed using the arithmetic mean and independent-samples t-tests. The pretest results indicated that the control group performed within the below-average range, while the experimental group performed within the average range. Posttest results showed improvements in both groups, with the experimental group achieving above-average scores. Statistical analysis further revealed that ICT-enhanced PBL significantly improved students' critical thinking skills compared with traditional instructional methods. The findings highlight the transformative role of ICT in vocational education, particularly its potential to promote critical thinking, active learning, and contextualized workplace safety training. The study recommends integrating ICT-enhanced PBL into TVL programs, equipping educators with the necessary ICT-based instructional competencies, and increasing investments in ICT infrastructure. Overall, this approach promotes a holistic set of competencies that combines technical proficiency with analytical thinking, thereby preparing vocational education for a dynamic and future-oriented transformation.

papers.title: Stereolithography-fabricated β-TCP and HAp TPMS scaffolds: mechanical and biological performance of sheet and solid-based lattices
papers.abstract: This study evaluates the mechanical and biological performance of Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) scaffolds (gyroid and diamond) in two different lattice topologies (sheet and solid-based) using calcium phosphate-based materials. While natural trabecular bone exhibits a compressive strength of 20–80 MPa, current synthetic scaffolds often struggle to balance structural integrity with bioactivity. We investigated sheet and solid-based TPMS lattice topologies at porosities of 65% and 50%, manufactured using stereolithography of hydroxyapatite (HAp) and beta-tricalcium phosphate (β-TCP) slurries. Mechanical testing showed that solid-based lattice topologies provided superior performance, reaching compression strengths of up to 20 MPa, with solid-based gyroid geometries consistently outperforming diamond structures at porosities above 50%. On the other hand, sheet-based geometries offered compression strength less than 10 MPa across both HAp and TCP. Biologically, while both HAp and β-TCP supported cell proliferation and exhibited similar initial alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, HAp demonstrated higher structural strength at the cost of lower long-term bone mineralization. In contrast, β-TCP facilitated higher mineralization, suggesting a faster rate of biological integration. These findings indicate that while solid gyroid HAp scaffolds provide compression strength analogous to trabecular bone, the integration of β-TCP is essential for long-term osteoblast mineralisation. This research provides a framework for optimizing the trade-off between mechanical resilience and biological functionality in the design of next-generation BTE implants.

papers.title: Knowledge-informed 3D Stochastic Geometry Gravity Inversion with FFT Acceleration
papers.abstract: Abstract Reconstructing three-dimensional (3D) geometric features is important for mineral exploration and development. However, most geophysical inversion studies focus on recovering physical properties, with less attention paid to geometric characteristics and associated uncertainty of the resulting models. Although the stochastic inversion framework has been widely used for uncertainty quantification, it still faces significant computational challenges. To address these issues, a 3D stochastic geometry gravity inversion framework accelerated by an FFT-based strategy is developed. Geological interfaces are represented by an implicit level-set function, and spatially correlated perturbations are generated in the frequency domain to improve sampling efficiency. Gravity observations, drillhole lithological constraints, and geological diagrams are integrated into a unified probabilistic objective function. Synthetic experiments show that the method reconstructs complex intrusion geometries with clearer boundaries than property-based inversion and provides spatial uncertainty estimates. Frequency-domain sampling achieves reconstruction accuracy comparable to spatial-domain sampling while reducing computation time to approximately one third. A robustness test further indicates that the framework can recover the main target geometry even when the geological diagram is biased. Application to the Olympic Dam deposit demonstrates that the method can construct geologically plausible 3D models and identify regions of higher structural uncertainty. This framework provides an efficient way to combine geophysical data and geological knowledge for uncertainty-aware geometry inversion.

papers.title: First-Principles and Machine Learning for Data-Driven Rational Design of High-Entropy Alloys: A Review
papers.abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) exhibit excellent comprehensive properties. Nevertheless, their complex multicomponent compositions and prevalent chemical short-range order (SRO) impose substantial obstacles to conventional trial-and-error-based development. This review systematically compares mainstream first-principles modeling approaches for disordered alloys, including the virtual crystal approximation (VCA), special quasirandom structures (SQS), coherent potential approximation (CPA), and hybrid Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics (MC/MD) simulations. We further summarize their applications in investigating the phase stability, plastic deformation, and functional performances of HEAs, such as catalytic behavior and hydrogen storage capacity. This work also classifies machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) into three generations: handcrafted descriptor-based potentials, system-specific E(3)-equivariant graph neural network potentials (represented by NequIP and Allegro), and universal pretrained potentials (exemplified by CHGNet and MACE). The respective advantages and limitations of these potentials for large-scale atomistic simulations concerning SRO and defects are elaborated. Furthermore, integrated alloy design strategies combining the CALPHAD method, active learning, and interpretable machine learning are introduced. Finally, critical bottlenecks, including dataset heterogeneity, insufficient model transferability, and low model interpretability, are identified. Future perspectives involving universal material foundation models and autonomous closed-loop discovery of alloys are also put forward. This review provides a systematic framework for the data-driven rational design of multi-principal element alloys.

papers.title: Projeto Escolas Inovadoras: práticas extensionistas e metodologias ativas na formação docente
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes and critically reflects on the contributions, scope, and limitations of the extension project “Innovative Schools: Active Learning Methodologies,” conducted from March 2024 to July 2025 as a continuing teacher education initiative. While the extension project aimed to provide teacher education in active methodologies and educational technologies, the purpose of this manuscript is to report, analyze, and critically discuss the training process and the outcomes perceived by participants. Developed by professors from the Mathematics Licentiate Degree at the Fluminense Federal University (UFF), together with scholarship holders and volunteers, the project involved approximately 120 teachers from Santo Antônio de Pádua, Miracema, Aperibé (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil), and Palma (Minas Gerais, Brazil). The analyzed records consisted of logbooks kept by the project team and electronic forms with open- and closed-ended questions, voluntarily answered by participants at the end of the modules. Thematic content analysis of the qualitative records indicated perceived expansion of teachers’ pedagogical repertoire, greater confidence in experimenting with active methodologies and technologies, and a demystified view of their use. Limitations related to technological infrastructure, working conditions, and the need for longitudinal follow-up were also identified. Since the study did not include systematic observation of classroom practices, the findings do not support claims of permanent changes in teaching practice or student learning.

papers.title: Active Fourier spectroscopy: From fixed sampling protocols to adaptive measurement
papers.abstract: Fourier-transform spectroscopy (FTS) is based on the Nyquist-Shannon theorem, which dictates a strict sampling protocol for the measurement of continuous signals. Here, we introduce active Fourier spectroscopy (AFS), a generalization of FTS in which measurements are still taken in the Fourier-conjugate delay domain, but where the most informative acquisition points are selected adaptively and the spectrum is reconstructed by sequential, uncertainty-aware inference rather than by fixed-grid Fourier inversion. Our approach relies on a theoretical insight that the Nyquist condition applies only under complete ignorance about the system under investigation, and shows how to systematically improve upon it when prior knowledge exists. AFS recovers conventional FTS when the prior is uninformative and falls back to it when prior knowledge is not supported by the data. We demonstrate AFS for optical spectroscopy in three settings vital to research and medicine: clinical FTIR (Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy)-based blood plasma analysis, optical metrology of structured laser beams, and hyperspectral imaging with an RGB camera. In each case, AFS reaches a higher target reconstruction quality from far fewer acquisitions and provides complete uncertainty quantification in real time, propagated rigorously through downstream analysis.

papers.title: Collaborative optimization analysis of thermal insulation and crack propagation in YSZ/(Y0.5Gd0.5)TaO4 double-ceramic-layer thick thermal barrier coating
papers.abstract: YSZ/(Y 0 . 5 Gd 0 . 5 )TaO 4 (YGT) double-ceramic-layer thermal barrier coatings (DCL-TBCs) are highly promising for advanced hot-section components in aero-engines and gas turbines. However, in thermal barrier coating (TBC) applications, an inherent trade-off exists between thermal insulation performance and structural integrity, necessitating collaborative optimization through coating structural design, particularly in thick coatings. To address this challenge, this study employs a finite element method (FEM) to systematically investigate the effects of thickness ratio and crack distribution on the thermomechanical behavior and crack propagation mechanisms of the TBC and to establish a collaborative optimization framework. Results show that when the YGT thickness ratio is controlled within 25%∼33%, the coating achieves an optimal balance between enhanced thermal insulation and reduced interfacial stress, enabling a favorable synergy between thermal performance and structural stability. At a crack density of 2.5 cracks/mm, both the YSZ/YGT interfacial and the oxide layer stress attain their minimum. A medium crack density (1.5∼4.5 cracks/mm) may efficiently reduce stress concentration at the crack tip via the stress shielding effect. When the crack spacing falls below 0.4 mm, propagation of the intermediate crack is suppressed, whereas at spacing exceeding 0.6 mm, the interaction between adjacent cracks is substantially weakened. Based on the results, a comprehensive optimization function is developed to identify the optimal design window for the YGT thickness ratio. This study offers theoretical guidance and evaluation methods for the collaborative optimization of the structural design and performance of high-reliability thick thermal barrier coatings (TTBC).

papers.title: A comprehensive survey of game theory models, applications, and future directions in cybersecurity
papers.abstract: This survey provides a comprehensive examination of game-theoretic solutions for cybersecurity, charting the field’s evolution from foundational models to the emerging paradigm of autonomous strategic defense. We systematize the literature by classifying core game-theoretic frameworks, including Stackelberg, Bayesian, and cooperative games, and examine their application to critical security tasks. For each model–application pairing, we grade the supporting evidence as theoretical, simulation-based, benchmark-based, or operationally deployed, showing that most cyber-domain approaches have not yet been validated in operational deployments. A central contribution of this work is a critical analysis of the theory–practice feedback loop, illustrated through in-depth case studies of seminal deployed physical-security systems such as ARMOR, PROTECT, and TRUSTS, whose lessons we relate to cyber defense. These examples reveal how real-world implementation challenges, including adversary bounded rationality and environmental uncertainty, have exposed the limitations of classical models and catalyzed fundamental advancements in the field. Building on this analysis, we synthesize the convergence of game theory and artificial intelligence, providing a structured examination of three critical frontiers: the strategic arms race in adversarial machine learning, the design of incentive-compatible security for federated learning, and the development of adaptive defense agents via multi-agent reinforcement learning in modern cyber gyms. Finally, we analyze the strategic challenges of collaborative security through the lens of dynamic coalition formation models. By identifying key research gaps and charting a forward-looking agenda, this survey aims to equip researchers and practitioners with a nuanced understanding of how to architect the next generation of intelligent, adaptive, and strategically robust cybersecurity systems.

papers.title: Model Predictive and FLC-MPPT Control for Hybrid Fuel Cell - Wind Power System
papers.abstract: Renewable energy sources are intermittent by nature, making it challenging to meet long-term energy demand reliably. One solution proposed by researchers is the integration of different energy sources into hybrid energy systems. This paper presents a hybrid energy system based on clean energy sources and proposes an energy management strategy to regulate power flow among the system components and meet load requirements. The paper investigates the control of a grid-connected hybrid renewable energy system comprising a 4 kW wind turbine and a 4.5 kW proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cell stack. Model predictive control (MPC) is employed to regulate the active and reactive power exchanged with the grid and to maximize the power extracted from the system's renewable energy sources. Maximum power point tracking (MPPT) for the fuel cell subsystem is achieved using a fuzzy logic-based controller. The hybrid system consists of two power electronic converters: an AC–DC converter, which connects the wind turbine subsystem to the DC bus, and a DC–AC inverter, which interfaces the DC bus with the grid. The MPC strategy selects the optimal inverter switching state by minimizing a cost function defined in terms of active and reactive power errors. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed control strategy.

papers.title: Media Pop-Up Book Berbasis Problem Based Learning Meningkatkan Hasil Belajar IPAS Siswa Sekolah Dasar
papers.abstract: The limited use of innovative learning media in elementary schools has contributed to students' low engagement and learning outcomes in Natural and Social Sciences. This study aimed to develop a Problem Based Learning-based Pop-Up Book and evaluate its validity, practicality, and effectiveness in improving fourth-grade students' learning outcomes. The study employed a Research and Development approach using the ADDIE model, which consists of Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation stages. The research was conducted in three elementary schools involving subject matter experts, media experts, language experts, teachers, and fourth-grade students. Data were collected through interviews, observations, validation sheets, practicality questionnaires, documentation, and learning achievement tests. The data were analyzed using descriptive quantitative techniques, while the effectiveness of the developed media was measured using the normalized gain score. The findings revealed that the developed media achieved an average validity score of 85.83%, indicating that it was valid for classroom use. The practicality assessment showed very practical criteria with scores of 95% from teachers and 87.4% from students. Furthermore, the effectiveness test demonstrated high normalized gain scores ranging from 0.81 to 0.90, indicating that the media effectively improved students' learning outcomes. These findings suggest that the developed Pop-Up Book provides an engaging and effective learning resource that supports active learning and enhances elementary students' understanding of Natural and Social Sciences.
