papers.title: A vision-based deep reinforcement learning control of windows and thermostats in naturally-ventilated building for environment management and energy conservation
papers.abstract: Occupant-Centric Control (OCC) strategies informed by Computer Vision (CV) offers opportunities for improving building energy performance and indoor environmental quality. However, coordinating natural ventilation and heating during winter remains challenging due to the trade-off between indoor air quality and ventilation-related heating losses caused by opening windows. Building upon our previous work, this study further explores the feasibility of integrating CV with a Deep Q-Network (DQN) window opening controller combined with occupancy-driven heating. First, real-time profiles of heat gains from occupants and window opening ratios were collected by utilizing CV cameras. Second, a Python–EnergyPlus co-simulation platform was developed. Third, a DQN controller that dynamically adjusted window openings, coupled with an occupancy-driven heating controller was proposed and subsequently trained through repeated interactions with the co-simulation platform. Eight simulation cases were designed to distinguish the individual and combined effects of the two controllers. Simulation results indicated that, in comparison to conventional scheduled heating and observed window-opening profiles, the combined controllers could reduce heating demand by 64.2%–65.2%, maintain near-neutral thermal comfort (−0.5 ≤ PMV ≤ 0.5) for 80.6%–93.8% of occupied time and achieve the proportion of occupied time which CO₂ concentrations remained below 1000 ppm for 99.3%-100%, while 87.5% for the baseline Cases. Future work should focus on its generalizability and performance against field measurements.

papers.title: Physics-informed frequency-domain inverse operator learning for moving dynamic load identification
papers.abstract: Moving-load identification from structural vibration responses is important for load assessment and monitoring of transportation infrastructure, where dynamic traffic loads are often difficult to measure directly. However, the problem is inherently ill-posed and is further complicated by the non-local cross-frequency coupling induced by load motion. To address this challenge, this study proposes a physics-informed frequency-domain inverse operator learning method that reformulates moving-load identification from sample-wise inversion into a reusable function-to-function inverse operator learning problem from acceleration responses to moving loads. An analytical forward operator is first constructed to explicitly capture motion-induced cross-frequency coupling, while a Fourier neural operator is used to learn the non-local inverse mapping from response to load. Rather than directly inverting the physical operator, the analytical operator is retained in the stable forward direction to map the predicted load back to the response space. Forward–inverse consistency is then imposed to constrain the learned inverse operator, enabling joint training with labelled load supervision and response-only physics supervision. The framework is evaluated progressively using a simply supported beam, a periodically supported beam, and a multi-wheelset train–track system, including response noise and parameter errors in the embedded physical operator. It is further applied to measured rail acceleration responses, where response reconstruction is used to assess field applicability. The results demonstrate stable identification across increasing structural complexity, noise, operator uncertainty, and broadband multi-wheelset excitation. The proposed framework provides a rapid and explicitly physics-constrained computational approach for response-based moving-load assessment in transportation infrastructure.

papers.title: LOCAL ADMINISTRATION OF TRANEXAMIC ACID IN PRIMARY CEMENTLESS TOTAL HIP ARTHROPLASTY: A PROSPECTIVE CONTROLLED CLINICAL STUDY
papers.abstract: Introduction: Perioperative blood loss and allogeneic transfusion remain important concerns in total hip arthroplasty. This study evaluated whether local intraoperative tranexamic acid reduces postoperative blood loss and transfusion requirements in primary cementless total hip arthroplasty. Material and Methods: In this prospective, single-center controlled study, 20 adults with hip osteoarthritis undergoing primary cementless total hip arthroplasty were allocated consecutively by an alternating method to an intervention group or control group (10 patients each). The intervention group received 2 g of tranexamic acid diluted in 60 mL of normal saline and administered locally in three 20-mL applications. Hematological parameters, postoperative drainage, and packed red blood cell transfusion requirements were recorded. Results: On postoperative day 5, mean hemoglobin was 112.3 g/L in the intervention group and 94.4 g/L in the control group (p=0.011), while mean hematocrit was 0.33 and 0.27, respectively (p=0.007). Mean drainage volume on the day of surgery was 239.5 mL versus 520.3 mL (p=0.002), and total drainage was 430.9 mL versus 755.4 mL (p=0.004). Two packed red blood cell units were transfused in the intervention group and 10 in the control group. Conclusion: Local intraoperative tranexamic acid was associated with higher postoperative hemoglobin and hematocrit values, lower measured drainage volume, and fewer transfused units. Interpretation of drainage outcomes is limited by different drain-activation protocols between groups. Keywords: Tranexamic Acid; Arthroplasty, Replacement, Hip; Blood Loss, Surgical; Blood Transfusion; Osteoarthritis, Hip

papers.title: Water-stable low-temperature porous boron nitride for dyes removal from wastewater: Insights on its material, adsorptive, stability and mechanistic aspects
papers.abstract: Ceramic-based boron nitride (BN) is marred with challenges like requirement of high fabrication temperatures and exhibiting poor aqueous phase stability. Another key aspect is its inability to remove anionic dyes from water. Low-temperature fabricated BN-900 was nano-rods; showed features coherent with a layered crystalline lattice structure, high surface functionality as well as high band gap typical of BN, but showing high disorderness, less crystallinity with more defects and mesoporosity. Under optimized conditions, BN-900 demonstrated 99% methyl green (MG) removal within 30 mins of contact, and its binding showed adherence to a monolayer with physisorption and demonstrated endothermicity. Another aspect is that BN-900 showed 75-95% removal for anionic dyes like Congo Red (CR), Methyl Orange (MO), and Eriochrome Black-T (EBT); a unique aspect not shown by other reported BN. Mechanistic aspect revealed an interplay of electrostatic attraction, hydrogen bonding, π-π interaction, Lewis acid-base and Van der Waals forces. Adequate stability for 3 weeks as well as high reusability was demonstrated by the BN-900 in this study. Further, demonstration of better MG removal under real wastewater conditions reveals the better potential of a low-temperature induced BN as an adsorbent.

papers.title: Does a fixed tensor-derived coordinate improve finite-grid Bayesian optimization? A matched-control evaluation
papers.abstract: Hyperparameter tuning often chooses from a fixed list of candidate settings with few evaluations. We ask whether a fixed tensor-derived transfer coordinate improves a finite-grid Bayesian optimizer that already starts from source-informed anchors. A matched-control procedure, built from established components, holds a Gaussian-process expected-improvement (GP–EI) backend, its source-derived anchors, and a target-information boundary fixed across three arms, and varies only the candidate representation: the coordinate, a distribution-matched permutation of it, or the plain grid. Comparing the coordinate with its permutation estimates the contribution of candidate association apart from adding a matched input. Over 96 scenario–task instances from 58 task identifiers and 30 seeds per arm (8,640 trajectories), the pooled full-trajectory (budget 3–50) normalized-AURC difference versus plain grid is − 0.001190 (95% CI [ − 0.004185 , 0.001534 ] ; clustered by task [ − 0.004046 , 0.001557 ] ): a 9.7% relative reduction in the mean, with an interval that neither establishes nor excludes a practically relevant benefit. Across margins from 5% to 35%, including an illustrative 15% margin, no margin establishes a benefit and nominal equivalence appears only at 30% or wider. More instances favor plain grid (47 against 27), and no contrast survives multiplicity correction, including in the sensitivity and matched anchor-count studies. The coordinate carries a measured 10.2% optimizer-CPU cost (about 0.53 seconds per run, excluding model training). The evidence is inconclusive rather than evidence of no effect: it does not support adopting the coordinate by default on the evaluated grids. One scenario (glmnet) shows a favorable exploratory association signal that remains unexplained.

papers.title: Microstructural evolution and mechanical and corrosion behavior of TIG-welded SLM/wrought 304 L stainless steel joints
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of selective laser melting (SLM) and wrought 304L stainless steel requires a better understanding of how manufacturing-induced microstructural differences affect weld performance. In this study, three TIG-welded joint configurations, SLM/SLM (SS), SLM/wrought (SW), and wrought/wrought (WW), were investigated to establish the relationships among substrate microstructure, weld solidification, tensile behavior, and corrosion resistance. Results revealed that solution-treated SLM and wrought substrates retained distinct crystallographic characteristics, which may influence grain selection near the fusion boundaries. Weld solidification was primarily governed by chemical composition and local solidification conditions, with measured δ-ferrite fractions increasing from 12.92 ± 0.98% (SS) to 14.73 ± 3.31% (SW) and 16.78 ± 4.68% (WW). The SS joint exhibited the highest yield strength (328.67 ± 3.21 MPa), whereas the WW joint achieved the highest ultimate tensile strength (677.85 ± 2.31 MPa). In contrast, the SW joint showed reduced tensile strength (608.03 ± 2.60 MPa) and elongation (40.84 ± 0.95%), accompanied by asymmetric microstructural characteristics. Electrochemical measurements revealed that the SS joint had the highest pitting potential (0.41 ± 0.03 V), while the SW joint exhibited the lowest (0.22 ± 0.04 V). These findings demonstrate that substrate-dependent microstructural characteristics and weld solidification behavior jointly influence the mechanical and corrosion responses of TIG-welded SLM/wrought 304L stainless steel joints.

papers.title: Intelligent forecasting and control of multi-microgrid systems via Large Language Models and Cloud–edge collaboration
papers.abstract: Energy management in interconnected microgrids requires numerical forecasts and operational information to be translated into coordinated decisions under physical constraints. This paper proposes a collaborative framework that connects interpretation by a large language model in the cloud with forecasting and predictive control at the edge. The cloud retrieves dated operating records and extracts event factors and effective tariffs from weather, calendar and policy notices. Numerical and source evidence checks govern their use in the controller. At the edge, a compact recurrent network with an attention mechanism forecasts load and photovoltaic generation, while a causal adapter incorporates accepted contextual factors into coordinated model predictive control. Evaluation using benchmark microgrids derived from measured power profiles shows lower cash operating costs and unserved energy than local edge control. Forecast errors pooled over the prediction horizon are also lower than those of a validation selected statistical baseline. With identical contextual information, language model and rule extraction yield similar dispatch outcomes, although the rule parser is more accurate. The framework establishes an explicit interface between contextual interpretation and constrained dispatch, while clarifying the contributions of coordination, forecasting and contextual extraction within the evaluated notice families.

papers.title: Covariance-Regulated Recursive Koopman Learning for Nonlinear Systems With Uncertain Time-Varying Dynamics
papers.abstract: Offline models for autonomous robots often fail under time-varying dynamics outside their training distribution. While Koopman operator theory offers a linear representation of nonlinear dynamics via lifting, its transition to online recursive estimation may suffer numerical vulnerabilities: covariance windup under low excitation when using exponential forgetting, and vanishing gain without forgetting. To prevent covariance explosion and parameter freezing, this paper introduces a unified Covariance-Regulated Recursive Koopman Learning (CR-RKL) framework that systematically incorporates and evaluates several covariance-regulated methods. Specifically, we propose a novel error dead-zone covariance skipping strategy, along with adaptations of constant-trace normalization and directional forgetting to the Koopman-specific setting. Validated on a non-holonomic differential-drive robot with wheel slip and Stribeck friction, as well as on a two-winged, tailless flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle, CR-RKL achieves numerically stable and accurate online modeling relative to its offline and vanilla recursive counterparts. When embedded in model predictive control, it maintains reliable tracking performance under uncertain, time-varying dynamics with bounded dictionaries. However, we also identify a structural limitation: while covariance-regulated methods achieve low off-policy prediction error, pairing them with unbounded dictionaries can lead to control failure.

papers.title: Infectious disease dynamics prediction and parameter identification by integrating graph neural networks and physics-informed neural networks
papers.abstract: The global spread of epidemics such as coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has highlighted the importance of high-accuracy forecasting and interpretable modeling. Traditional mechanistic models often suffer from limited predictive performance under complex real-world conditions, whereas purely data-driven methods generally lack epidemiological interpretability. Existing approaches, however, largely neglect the spatial dependencies of infectious disease transmission across regions. Therefore, achieving both accurate prediction and interpretable estimation of epidemiological parameters remains a critical challenge in epidemic modeling and forecasting. In this study, we propose a novel epidemic modeling framework that integrates graph neural networks (GNNs) with a discrete-time physics-informed neural network (PINN). The GNN module characterizes cross-regional spatial dependencies by aggregating epidemiological information from neighboring regions, while the PINN module explicitly embeds the dynamical constraints of the discretized SIR equations into the graph-structured learning process. By jointly optimizing the data-fitting loss, discrete-time dynamical residual loss, and initial-condition loss, the framework aims to improve predictive accuracy while promoting consistency with the underlying epidemiological dynamics. Through this synergistic design, neural networks can effectively identify physically meaningful transmission parameters, including infection rate and recovery rate. Experimental results on multi-level COVID-19 datasets demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over existing baselines, along with its capability for effective parameter identification.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural networks for simulating nonlinear Powell–Eyring nanofluid flow dynamics with comparative analysis
papers.abstract: This study develops a hybrid physics-informed neural network (PINN) and RK4-shooting framework for the coupled momentum, heat, and nanoparticle transport of a chemically reactive Powell–Eyring nanofluid over an inclined stretching cylinder. The model incorporates magnetohydrodynamic forcing, the Buongiorno Brownian-motion and thermophoretic mechanisms, thermal radiation, viscous dissipation, stress-based velocity slip, activation energy, chemical reaction, and Cattaneo–Christov non-Fourier heat flux. Similarity variables reduce the boundary-layer equations to nonlinear ordinary differential equations, which are solved first by a fourth-order Runge–Kutta shooting scheme and then embedded in a PINN through momentum, energy, concentration, and boundary-condition residuals. Across the tabulated wall-response cases, the maximum relative discrepancy between PINN and RK4 predictions is below 0.082%, demonstrating close cross-method agreement. The computations show that the magnetic field retards axial motion through Lorentz resistance, radiation and viscous dissipation elevate temperature, and thermophoresis and activation energy substantially modify nanoparticle concentration. Increasing curvature decreases the thermal and concentration fields through enhanced geometric spreading. The framework provides a physics-constrained surrogate for rapid prediction within the investigated parameter ranges.

papers.title: Does AI Personalization Add Value to Project-Based Learning? A Quasi-Experimental Study of Undergraduate Students’ Critical Thinking Skills
papers.abstract: Purpose: This study examines whether integrating AI personalization into a Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model produces an incremental effect on undergraduate students' critical thinking skill beyond that generated by PjBL alone, addressing the underexamined question of whether AI personalization can meaningfully intervene in critical thinking development once a pedagogically robust active-learning model is already in place. Methods: A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control group design was employed involving 88 third-semester Business Education students at Universitas Negeri Malang, The study utilized two pre-existing classes, assigned to groups receiving either conventional PjBL (n = 46) or the PjBL learning model with AI personalization (n = 42). Data were analyzed using Wilcoxon Signed-Rank and Mann-Whitney U tests with N-Gain scoring. Findings: Both conditions improved significantly with large within-group effects (control: 70.98 to 89.91, N-Gain = 0.63, Z = −5.91, p < .001, r = 0.87; experimental: 73.14 to 89.79, N-Gain = 0.60, Z = −5.64, p < .001, r = 0.87). Neither the between-group posttest comparison (U = 886.00, Z = -0.72, p = 0.471, r = 0.08) nor the comparison of N-Gain scores (U = 840.50, Z = -1.06, p = 0.292, r = 0.11) reached significance, and the direction of both differences favored the control condition. Experiment group therefore produced no detectable advantage over control group in this setting. Research Implications: Both conditions delivered individualised, criterion-referenced formative feedback organised by the same criteria, differing only in its source, which may explain the absence of a detectable difference. The study found no evidence that AI-supported feedback was superior to peer-supported feedback under the conditions examined; these results do not establish that the two approaches are equivalent. Originality: This study examines a configuration that has received relatively little research attention: AI-based personalization integrated into established active learning models. It evaluates and compares different active learning models against one another, rather than contrasting them with passive learning. The study proposes the concept of a “pedagogical sufficiency threshold” as a testable framework for determining when AI adds substantive value to a learning model, rather than merely introducing redundancy.

papers.title: Machine learning-guided discovery of TMX 4 @G electrocatalysts with LLM-assisted workflow automation
papers.abstract: Coordination-engineered transition-metal single-atom catalysts offer a modular platform for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), but their discovery is hindered by the large configurational space arising from coupled metal-ligand variations. Here we develop a symmetry-aware and uncertainty-guided workflow to accelerate the screening of TMX4@G catalysts (X = C, N, O, P or S), where a transition-metal atom is coordinated by four ligands embedded in graphene. Canonicalization of rotationally equivalent motifs reduces 17 500 nominal structures to 4900 symmetry-inequivalent candidates while preserving chemical diversity. A cascaded Gaussian process regression model encodes a physical hierarchy from atomic descriptors to electronic structure, metal-hydrogen interaction and the HER activity. Posterior uncertainty drives active learning by balancing near-thermoneutral hydrogen binding with exploration of underrepresented coordination motifs. A large language model (LLM)-assisted automation framework further integrates structure generation, VASP input preparation, job submission, output parsing and dataset updating. DFT validation shows strong agreement with model predictions (R2 = 0.898 for 24 candidates) and identifies six thermodynamically stable catalysts with ηHER < 0.15 V.

papers.title: Influence of FSP travel orientation relative to the LPBF build direction on microstructural evolution, defect formation, and mechanical response of Ti-6Al-4V
papers.abstract: Friction stir processing (FSP) was applied to heat-treated Ti-6Al-4V fabricated by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) at three FSP travel orientations (0°, 45°, and 90°) relative to the fixed LPBF build direction to determine how relative directional alignment influences microstructural evolution and the resulting physical and mechanical response. Microstructure, X-ray diffraction (XRD), hardness, electrical resistivity, tensile properties, processing-induced defects, and fracture morphology were evaluated. Relative to the heat-treated (HTed) reference condition, FSP produced a finer, predominantly equiaxed stir-zone morphology in all three configurations. XRD showed changes in relative α(α′) peak intensities and apparent peak widths after FSP. The maximum mean transverse hardness values were approximately 414, 421, and 416 HV for the 0°, 45°, and 90° configurations, respectively, after FSP. Electrical resistivity increased relative to the corresponding HTed condition at all three orientations. When averaged across the three orientations, mean UTS increased from 1046 MPa in the HTed condition to 1154 MPa after FSP, while mean failure strain decreased from 12.2% to 5.6%. Two-way ANOVA showed significant Processing × Orientation interactions for electrical resistivity and failure strain, but not for YS or UTS, indicating a property-specific orientation response. Local void-like defects and embedded tungsten fragments were observed in selected processed specimens, although the defect assessment remained qualitative. FSP produced substantial microstructural and property changes, while the influence of relative orientation depended on the measured property.

papers.title: Digital Twin Protocol for Adaptive Power Distribution in Simulated Rack-Level Direct Current Systems Under Graphics Processing Unit Load Surges
papers.abstract: Rapid changes in graphics processing unit (GPU) demand motivate coordinated control of power supply units (PSUs) and uninterruptible power supplies (UPSs). This protocol describes a digital twin framework for a simulated 54 V direct current (DC) rack, combining a two-layer gated recurrent unit (GRU), model predictive control (MPC), and recursive least squares (RLS). Independent Python plant integration and an analytical predictor operate at a 0.25 s supervisory interval with 20 prediction intervals and explicit storage-energy accounting. Four synthetic workload scenarios and five paired realizations compare idealized static allocation, reactive control, conventional MPC, forecast-informed fixed-model MPC, and adaptive MPC. Additional tests impose forecast bias, PSU parameter shifts, sensor noise, and delayed commands. Voltage metrics retain 1 ms integration points. Relative to conventional MPC initialized with a mismatched PSU time constant, adaptive MPC reduces RMS voltage error and storage depletion in the three surge scenarios. It does not improve every metric or establish superiority over reactive control. Endpoint-only constraints permit intersample voltage excursions. Future-only forecast errors are reported against persistence, although overlapping GRU training windows limit the independence of the model's test error. Voltage error, out-of-band duration, PSU loading, storage throughput, and numerical-loop latency define the evaluation. Converter dynamics, local protection, independent workload validation, and physical deployment require further study.

papers.title: Improving multi-class image classification accuracy through hyper-parameter tuning of convolutional neural networks
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major global health challenge, particularly in low-resource settings where early diagnosis is critical for reducing mortality rates. Colposcopy-based screening is widely used for detecting cervical abnormalities; however, accurate multi-class classification of cervical images remains difficult due to severe class imbalance, high intra-class variability, and sensitivity of convolutional neural network (CNN) models to hyperparameter settings. To address these challenges, this study investigates the combined effect of data augmentation and hyperparameter optimization on improving cervical image classification performance. Specifically, a conditional Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Network (DCGAN) is employed to synthesize minority class samples and balance the dataset. The experiments are conducted on the Intel-MobileODT Cervical Cancer Screening dataset, which contains 1,481 images across three classes with significant imbalance. The quality of generated images is evaluated using the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) metric. Further, multiple CNN architectures—including a baseline CNN, a compact custom CNN, and a multi-scale fused CNN—are evaluated before and after hyperparameter tuning using GridSearchCV, with Bayesian optimization considered as part of an ablation study. The optimized Fused CNN achieved an average accuracy of 85.4% based on five-fold cross-validation. In addition, independent test-set evaluations on datasets of increasing size yielded higher category-wise accuracy of 87.85%, 96.00%, and 97.23%, reflecting improved performance with larger training data. Additionally, ablation analysis confirms that DCGAN-based augmentation effectively mitigates overfitting in minority classes. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of integrating data augmentation with systematic hyperparameter optimization to enhance the robustness and reliability of medical image classification systems in real-world clinical scenarios.

papers.title: Nonlinear data normalisation for reliable spatial inference with variational Gaussian processes
papers.abstract: Machine learning methods for grade estimation have been rising in popularity in recent years. Among these, the variational Gaussian process model possesses all the beneficial characteristics of the kriging estimator: conditioning on data, declustering properties, and an uncertainty measure that increases with distance from the data points. However, its use requires a transformation of the data to a Gaussian distribution, especially if the data is compositional, as is the case with drillhole assays. This work explores some transformations that were specifically adapted for this model, making use of principal components analysis, independent components analysis, monotonic splines, and flow methods. Results show that the best transformation is case-dependent, and that they provide similar results to the ones used for geostatistical simulation. An open-source implementation of the methods is available to the community.

papers.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Deep Neural Network Framework with Adaptive Representation Fusion for Secure IoT Data Transmission
papers.abstract: The rapid growth in the number of IoT devices has brought several security challenges, especially in the presence of network-based attacks. These attacks can disrupt the normal functioning of IoT networks and even result in financial losses through unauthorized access and information loss. Due to this, accurately detecting malicious network traffic is imperative for maintaining a secure IoT network. However, the increasing volume and complexity of network traffic make it increasingly difficult to categorize between normal and malicious traffic, creating a need for effective intrusion detection methods to identify various types of intrusions with high classification accuracy. This study proposes a QHCDN-IoT, Quantum-Hybrid Classical Deep Network for intelligent intrusion detection in IoT environments. The proposed framework aims to identify different categories of network traffic by learning both classical and quantum-based feature representations. To achieve this, the input network traffic data is initially preprocessed to improve its quality and consistency. Following that, the Correlation-based Feature Selection method is used to select relevant features while reducing redundant information. The selected features are then processed through parallel Deep Neural Network and Variational Quantum Neural Network branches to learn classical and quantum-based representations. An adaptive quantum-classical fusion module is subsequently used to combine the learned representations for intrusion classification. Bayesian Optimization is applied to identify suitable model hyperparameters, while Integrated Gradients is incorporated to explain the classification predictions by identifying the contribution of individual input features. To assess the performance of the proposed QHCDN-IoT framework, experimental analysis is conducted using the BoT-IoT and TON_IoT datasets. The proposed QHCDN-IoT achieved 94.67% accuracy and 93.50% F1-score on TON_IoT, and 94.59% accuracy and 93.65% F1-score on BoT-IoT.

summary_en.motivation: The growing scale and complexity of IoT traffic demand more accurate detection of malicious network activity.
summary_en.method: Parallel classical deep neural network and variational quantum neural network branches are fused adaptively, with Bayesian hyperparameter optimization and Integrated Gradients explanations.
summary_en.result: The framework reaches roughly 94.6% accuracy and 93.6% F1-score on two IoT intrusion datasets.
summary_en.validation: Performance is evaluated through classification experiments on the BoT-IoT and TON_IoT benchmark datasets.
